### D13 — Workspace context (rules, skills, memory) follows Muse Code's own conventions and VS Code's workspace trust (2026-09-22)

VS Code's workspace trust is the one switch for rules, skills and memory, on
both backends. In a trusted workspace the CLI is spawned with
`--trust-workspace` and the Model API backend loads the same things itself. In
Restricted Mode neither backend loads rules, skills or memory, and neither
runs shell commands. On the Model API backend the extension is the host, so it
mirrors Muse Code's conventions and no others: no invented file names, no
`MUSE.md`. The CLI names no agent folder, so M76's custom-agent folder is the
extension's own, the one place an invented name is allowed. The saved-plan
location is Muse Code's own, not the extension's. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D14 — Production hardening set for 0.2.0 (2026-09-22)

An audit of the tree for 0.2.0 produced a hardening list in which each item is
either done in M11 or recorded as deferred with its reason. The extension
declares `extensionKind: ["workspace"]`. An error boundary around the app
shows the message and a Reload button. Model API sessions are kept in a JSON
session store under `context.storageUri`, per workspace. `Muse Spark:
Diagnostics` writes support facts to the log, and nothing secret is ever
written. A publish job runs `vsce publish` only when the `VSCE_PAT` repository
secret exists. There is no telemetry, by design. The first workspace folder is
the root. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D20 — Replying to an output and quoting the chat (2026-09-22, night)

A reply or a quote reaches the agent as a `<chat_reference>` part that rides
before the editor context: a lead sentence naming the intent and the author,
then the passage in a fenced block, clipped at 8,000 characters with a note.
The transcript shows the typed text plus a chip. Each finished reply gets a
hover actions menu beside Copy with "Reply to this output", which sets the
composer's reference chip; the whole reply text is the payload. A right-click
with a non-empty selection inside a transcript row opens a small menu with
"Ask about this" and "Comment on this"; without a selection the browser menu
is untouched. There is one reference at a time: a new Reply or quote replaces
it, and it clears on send or when removed. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

run harness:shots`), and the integration tests in a real VS Code. It
establishes that `subagent_spawn` is an approval-gated tool; its card says
"use `subagent_spawn`" and its row is labelled "Spawn agent". The reducer
routes any item whose turn is a subagent's child session into that agent's
transcript in the map. `AgentSession.controlSubagent` and `messageSubagent`
exist on both hosts for the map's owner controls. The round raises the
reply-only live drill's model-attempt budget after three measurements. With
the `VSCE_PAT` repository secret set, the release workflow publishes every
later tag itself. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D22 — Issue #4: the prompt box grows with wrapped lines (2026-09-23)

D22 records the first community issue, that the chat input box only displays a
single line when the input gets longer, and its fix. The textarea's rows had
come from the newline count, so a long line that wrapped stayed one row. Now
`rowsFor(draft, metrics)` takes the content height in rows when the box can be
measured, else the newline count, and `fitRows` sets one row, measures and
sets the rows, from a layout effect on the draft and from a `ResizeObserver`
when the width changes. The cap stays `COMPOSER_MAX_ROWS` (ten); past it the
textarea scrolls inside. The composer therefore has the same shape as VS
Code's chat input: one row, growth, ten rows, internal scroll, verified in the
harness scenarios `composer-grow` and `composer-max`. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D23 — Rewind across subagents (2026-09-23)

D23 records a reader's question about rewind when several subagents touch
overlapping files, the gap it exposed and the fix. Rewind works per edit, with
no git: patches are unwound newest first, each hunk checked against the file.
Because a subagent's rows live in `childTranscripts`, `editsAfter` never saw
them and a delegated run's edits survived a rewind. `UiState.sequence`, a
monotonic arrival counter, now gives user cards a `seq` and tool rows a
`completedSeq`, and `editsAfter(state, messageId)` gathers the completed edit
rows of the conversation and of every child transcript past the message's
`seq`, newest first, so overlapping edits from any agent unwind in the reverse
of the order they landed on disk. The rewind undoes everything after a point,
and `revertHunks` refuses a file that no longer matches, with a notice,
instead of guessing. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D24 — The audit: security and confinement (2026-09-23)

D24 records Section A (security, M21) of the audit the owner asked for; the
audit's other sections are M22 to M26, recorded in D25 to D29. Its standing
rules: paths are confined with `confineWorkspacePath`, the textual check and
then the same check on the canonical forms; no git runs while the workspace is
untrusted; a protected write asks in every mode but Bypass (Plan refuses), and
session rules never cover it; `compileGlob` matches globs with no regular
expression; shell rules are keyed on the exact command line, only `allow_once`
/ `allow_session` approve, and an unknown id is rejected; turning
`allowDangerouslySkipPermissions` off moves every controller out of Bypass;
and in a remote window a conversation never starts in Bypass, and entering it
needs a modal yes once per conversation. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D25 — The audit: processes and lifecycle (2026-09-23)

Section B of the audit (D24), plus the lifecycle rows of section G, records
process and lifecycle findings with the change made for each. The standing
rules: `runCommand` makes POSIX commands lead their own process group and
kills the group, while each Windows command joins a named job object that Stop
and timeouts end with `TerminateJobObject`; before a restart each controller
remembers its session and the next message resumes it (`resumeAfterRestart`),
on the same backend kind only; `withDeadline` allows 30 s for the handshake,
60 s per command and 180 s for resume, fork, read and compact, and a process
still running at 30 s gets one longer wait, 120 s in all; a synthetic
`turnCompleted` ends the turn after a mid-turn death, restart or sign-out; and
handles are reference-counted on both backends. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D26 — The audit: protocol and backend semantics (2026-09-23)

D26 records the audit's Section C (D24) findings on protocol and backend
semantics with their fixes, then amendments on the SDK 1.4.4 re-check, Windows
limits, the CLI's sign-in, approval decisions and CLI recovery. Among its
standing rules, `finishCall` records an output for every tool call. The
Windows limits on rename and fork and D12's profile-workspace warning apply to
every version, lifted only by a release after a Muse Code version is verified
to fix them. The CLI's sign-in is read, not assumed. A second decision for an
approval stage is never sent, and a waiting approval's card is docked above
the composer. A session marked damaged by an event-log fault is never resumed
by itself, and the extension's delete port (`MuseCodeHost.deleteSession`) must
not be wired for 1.4.4 hosts. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

**Amendment 2026-10-09 (SDK144): re-checked against Muse Code SDK 1.4.4
and CLI 1.4.4-R5419.1.** Each workaround above was compared with the 1.4.4
source and the upstream issue (`docs/certification/sdk144.md` has the table).

- A resume parks the turn with no card: re-checked against 1.4.4, still
  needed. The SDK's read loop is unchanged, so a server request in the same
  read still reaches the handler before the awaiting command resumes.
- The handshake facts are dropped: re-checked against 1.4.4, still needed.
  Rename and fork on Windows (#30, #31, both open) were not retested (no
  Windows CLI in this lane); the limits stay on every version.
  C-M53-1 subsequently retested 1.4.4-R5419.1 on Win11 (2026-10-10):
  rename reports naming unavailable (`unsupported_platform` in the trace),
  and forks still return `forkBoundaryInvalid` / `WriteFailed`, with and
  without a cut, across concurrent hosts and after close/resume. TUI
  `/fork` fails too. The all-version Windows limit therefore stays;
  captures and the counted token-free echo runs are in `m53.md`.
- The 10 MiB frame cap: re-checked against 1.4.4, still needed. The SDK
  limits inbound frames only; an oversized outbound command is still
  written and never answered.
- `session/list` over its maximum: re-checked against 1.4.4, still needed
  (the schema still says "Maximum 200").
- The SDK keeps every command for ever (#35, open): partly fixed in 1.4.4
  (FR-45137-1). `Connection.command` now remembers a SHA-256 of each command
  and ack, not the payload, but still never forgets an entry. `sendCommand`
  stays: each attempt is also fenced by the host generation and heard by the
  watchdog, which `Connection.command` cannot do.
- 1.4.4 removes `session/delete` and `session/deleteCompleted` from MSP.
  1.4.4-R5419.1 answers `session/delete` with `methodNotFound` (probe,
  2026-10-09, zero model attempts). The extension's delete port
  (`MuseCodeHost.deleteSession`, lane W's lifecycle reader) is not wired in
  production, so nothing user-visible breaks; it must not be wired for
  1.4.4 hosts.

**Amendment 2026-10-19 (PR250FIX2, lane K activation budget).** The Muse
Code delete offer (`canDeleteMuseSession`: CLI version plus the injected
lifecycle reader) must stay out of the activation graph: `HostInfo`
carries `canDeleteSessions?`, a Muse Code host omits it, and the gate lives
in `src/core/backends/musecode/museDeleteGate.ts`, which no module the
activation bundle includes may import. A sync constructor cannot serve a
dynamic import, so the offer moved instead of the code; the reader
injection wires the offer when it lands. History offers Delete on Muse Code
nowhere until then, and nothing the CLI cannot answer is ever sent.

The workarounds recorded elsewhere, re-checked the same day:

### D27 — The audit: editing correctness (2026-09-23)

Section D of the audit (D24) records findings and changes for the Model API's
file tools, Edit Review and the context the agent reads. The standing rules:
hunks use unified numbering; a file counts as created only when nothing is
left once the edit is taken out; a file that has moved on is refused with the
reason, refined in D31 so that intact lines that only moved are found where
they moved to if they occur once; `edit_file` writes a file back in its own
line breaks and BOM; `readFile` refuses invalid UTF-8 or a NUL; the tools
refuse a file with unsaved changes; `write_file` replaces an existing file
only as the model last read or wrote it; and the context loaders confine
repository files by canonical path (`confineWorkspacePath`). Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D28 — The audit: webview and UI state (2026-09-23)

Section E of the audit (D24) records the findings on the webview's state and
its rendering, and M25 fixes them all in the webview. The standing rules it
establishes: the panel's state lives in a store outside the error boundary
(`state/store.ts`), saved to VS Code's webview state at most once a second and
at once before a reload; `completeTurn` settles the conversation's rows, so
streaming stops and a running tool that is not backgrounded becomes
`interrupted`; `clear()` posts `conversationCleared`; the composer's keys
return first for `isComposing`; a late `turnAccepted` marks the card sent and
starts nothing (`lastCompletedTurnId`); `sendFailed` carries
`attachmentsKept`, which decides whether the chips come back to the composer;
and `questionSubmitted` locks the question card until the host settles the
question. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D29 — The audit: packaging, CI, platform and voice (2026-09-23)

D29 records the fixes for section F of the audit (D24), row A5 on the release
workflow's secret scope, the two voice rows of section B and section G's
`windowsHide` rule for the spawns M26 owns. By the owner's ruling the macOS
helper is not signed or notarised; it stays ad-hoc signed, and the product
explains what macOS does with it. The standing changes include `win` key
bindings with Alt and tests that reject reserved chords; third-party notices
generated from metafiles, shipped and checked by the build; dictation refused
when the host is remote; an audit that stays blocking, with reviewed
exceptions expiring within 90 days; job timeouts everywhere they are allowed
and `persist-credentials: false`; and `VSCE_PAT` narrowed from job-level env
to the `verify` job, flag only, in one step after `--ignore-scripts`. Full
record: [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D30 — What we can build now, and Remote Control (2026-09-24)

Remote Control waits for Meta: remote use happens inside Meta's own apps, with
no phone or web app of ours. Paid features (M33–M35) are opt in and loud: off
by default with the price in the setting, confirmed when turned on, visibly on
with a badge, announced per use, and tallied in Account & usage. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

**Owner ruling on paid features (2026-09-24):** "for the api extrase we
could use the muse speach to text as well but any thing that costs needs to
be opt in and loud so the user never inadvertently uses token spend without
knowing". This supersedes the M9 rule of no API cost for speech-to-text, but
only for a paid engine the user turns on; the free OS recognisers stay the
default. The owner then answered two questions:

- **Where:** paid voice is offered on the Model API backend only, so the
  key is only ever spent on the key backend (D1 amendment, the billing
  ruling).
  - **The owner's reason:** "i dont think you can do api key and
    subscription at the same time on the same account".
  - **What Meta's Subscriptions page says (2026-09-24):** both can exist on
    one account, but the subscription "applies to the Muse Code API key
    that is automatically connected in the Muse Code CLI onboarding … for
    use with Muse Code only. Any additional API keys you create … will be
    billed through pay-as-you-go."
  - **So the ruling stands on either reading:** the subscription can never
    pay for Muse Voice, and any key the extension used would be
    pay-as-you-go.
  - **For later:** the subscription plans include voice mode and web search
    inside Muse Code itself, the free path for the Muse Code backend if
    Meta exposes them over MSP (watch item W4).
- **Bypass:** paid calls ask even in Bypass, which skips file and command
  prompts only, never a paid call.

Every paid feature (M33, M34, M35) must therefore be:

1. **Off by default**, with the price in its setting's description.
2. **Confirmed when turned on**: one modal naming the price, whether it is
   turned on from the panel or in settings (a declined confirmation turns
   the setting back off).
3. **Visibly on**: a badge in the composer footer names every paid feature
   that is on, with its price in the tooltip.
4. **Announced per use**: a paid call shows in the transcript as its own
   row marked paid. Image generation asks before each image, in every mode.
5. **Tallied**: the Account & usage dialog shows this window's count of each
   paid call and its estimated cost at the published prices.

### D31 — Rewind finds a hunk that only moved (2026-09-24)

A reader of our Bluesky thread asked whether a hand edit in the same lines
trips the rewind's skip, or whether the patch gets a fuzzy apply first. The
code's answer was: the same skip, no fuzzy apply. `revertHunks` matched each
hunk's lines exactly, but only at the line the edit recorded. So lines the
user merely added _above_ an edit, which leave its text intact, made the
rewind skip it too. That case was stricter than it needed to be, and D27's
row "a file that has moved on is refused" had pinned it.

**Owner's go-ahead (2026-09-24):** "yes fix it". The change refines D27 and
keeps its rule that nothing is guessed:

A reader asked whether a hand edit in the same lines rewind misses; it does
not. The owner's go-ahead (2026-09-24): yes, fix it. A moved hunk is matched
exactly, never guessed. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D32 — An accessibility gate: WCAG 2.2 AA with axe-core, in VS Code's own themes (2026-09-24)

The accessibility gate runs axe-core itself rather than Lighthouse. It checks
every harness scenario in each of VS Code's four default themes against axe's
WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 rules at levels A and AA, colour contrast included. Any
violation, or a page that reports no result, fails the gate, and what axe
files under "incomplete" fails like a violation, except contrast axe could not
see and glyph-only content, which are counted and printed. Two exemptions
stand: a `target-size` finding on a target obscured by a menu, popover or
dialog the user opened, and a `scrollable-region-focusable` finding on a
region whose listbox a focused or focusable element drives through
`aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`. The gate runs in `npm run
quality` and `quality:ci`, and in CI on Linux and Windows but not on macOS.
Full record: [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D33 — The panel in VS Code's display languages (2026-09-25)

The panel is translated into the fourteen languages VS Code itself ships; the
translations are machine-made, and the README says so. Text sits in two
tables: `MODEL_TEXT` holds what the model or Meta reads and stays English
whatever the display language, and `UI_TEXT` is what the user reads and is the
one translated. A spliced sentence becomes one template with named slots
filled by `fill(template, values)`, and a count-dependent string is an entry
of plural forms that `plural(entry, count)` picks with
`Intl.PluralRules(locale)`. English stays in `src/shared/l10n/en.ts`; the
fourteen others are JSON files in `l10n/`, shipped in the package and not
bundled. The manifest moves to `package.nls.json` and
`package.nls.<language>.json`. The gate `scripts/check-l10n.mjs`, in
`quality:gates`, checks every language against English. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D34 — The paid features, as built (2026-09-25)

The owner said "do it" (2026-09-25) to M33-M35 under D30's five rules: the
paid features (web search, image generation, voice transcription) sit behind
the paid gate — a feature is on only while its setting is on and the price was
accepted, acceptances live in the extension's global state, and the
subscription never pays. Prices and wire shapes were read from Meta's public
pages on 2026-09-25; the code's tariffs and the paid gate are the record
since. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D35 — Replay as Meta validates it (2026-09-25)

A full read of Meta's Model API documentation for the parity audit
found the Model API backend breaking three of the documented rules for a
conversation replayed by the client (protocols/responses, "Conversation
structure", "Message phase", "Reasoning item ordering"; error-handling,
"Invalid conversation structure"). None had been seen live: the owner has
held no key since 2026-09-22, and the fake API followed our own assumptions.

Replay as Meta validates it: a full read of the Model API documentation for
the parity audit found two wrong items (code execution and web search): both
are fixed, and two missing retry rules were added. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

Two retry rules were missing too (error-handling): a 502 is retried like the
other server errors (a 504 still is not: every long request streams), and a
stream that ends with an `error` event of `server_shutting_down`,
`service_overloaded` or `backend_unavailable` is sent again whole, with the
turn's retry notice; what the cut-short stream showed stays in the
transcript (a search row cut short reads "interrupted" and is not counted),
and only the retried response is replayed.

| Voice                             | the OS recogniser (free); Muse Code's live dictation is TUI-only and unavailable on Windows; 1.4.2 also has `muse voice transcribe <file>` outside MSP                                                    | the OS recogniser, or Muse Voice (paid, M35)                                                                                                       | —                   |
| Everything else already at parity | sessions, history, fork, rename, compaction, export, steering, queue, approvals with stages and scopes, questions, todos, usage, model, effort, modes, skills, rules, worktrees, attachments, diagnostics | the same, through the extension's own harness                                                                                                      | —                   |

Rulings carried: the subscription never pays for a Model API call, and the
key is never handed to `muse serve` (D1); a paid call is opt in and loud
(D30). Images on the Muse Code backend therefore run through the extension's
own session MCP server (the `ide` server Muse Code already loads, M5) with
the key, billed and announced exactly as on the Model API backend (M44).
What Muse Code keeps to its TUI and cannot be reached over MSP (its theme,
keymap, vim mode, HUD, deep research, live voice dictation) is listed and
not imitated, except where the panel has its own equivalent. Since 1.4.2,
`feedback/submit` is available to MSP clients granted the `feedback`
capability; the extension does not request it or upload feedback. Adding
that feature requires a privacy decision. File transcription is a CLI
command, not an MSP method.

### D37 — The key's paid features on the Muse Code backend (2026-09-25)

On the Muse Code backend images come from the extension: the `ide` session
server every Muse Code session already loads offers `generateImage` and
`editImage` while image generation is on (D30) and a Model API key is stored,
and the extension makes the image itself with the key. The key never reaches
`muse serve`, and the subscription never pays for an image. Muse Code's own
approval covers using the tool; the extension's modal covers buying the image,
and declining refuses the call and buys nothing. Account & usage, the badge
and the palette show the key's features on Muse Code while a key is stored:
images and Muse Voice, not web search. Image edits join generation under the
same setting, gate and price on both backends. The tool list is read per
request. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D38 — Session goals on both backends (M45, 2026-09-25)

M45 puts session goals on both backends. On Muse Code, `session/goalChanged`
and the resumed snapshot's goal reach the panel. The Model API backend gets
Muse Code's four tools with its argument names, rules, failure messages and
result shape; Stop pauses an active goal, and the user's verbs follow MSP's
rules and refusals. On purpose it has no turn of its own after a turn and no
completion audit, because each would be a model call billed to the key.
`/goal` in the prompt is a command, never a message. The PR reviews and audits
recorded afterwards add corrections to M45, among them that each Model API
request retains the revision of user goal commands at its start and that the
store defers any snapshot with an unanswered function call. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D40 — Workflows: captured read-only run card and setting (2026-09-25)

A Muse Code workflow item becomes its own row kind, a read-only card. The card
outlives its turn: it is never settled as interrupted when the turn ends. The
panel offers no workflow owner buttons or callable control path yet; before a
follow-up enables them, their live success shapes and outcome events must be
captured, the ack validated and source-session ownership enforced. The
Workflow tool row does not interpret an input `scriptPath`, and the card does
not parse, carry forward or display a `phase`, until a live capture
establishes them. `run.workflow_trigger_mode` is read from Muse Code's
settings file and reads `auto` when unset. A workflow spends the subscription
like any turn, so it is not a paid feature under D30. The Model API backend
has no workflow run to show. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D44 — Versions stay below 1.0 until the owner calls it (2026-09-25)

The owner (2026-09-25): "i dont think a 1.0 would be right until the app
has been on the market and field tested for a while … stay under that 1.0
mark until im confident the app is worthy of being called the first full
version". He suggested a fourth number (0.8.0.1); the Marketplace and
`vsce` accept only a three-part semantic version, so:

The owner (2026-09-25): no 1.0 until the app is ready; the minor counts past
nine, patch counts fixes back in time, and releases bunch by four-day train
windows. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D39 — Background work, the user's own shell, explanations, on both backends (2026-09-25)

On both backends the command Muse Spark: Move Running Command to Background is
bound to `ctrl+b` on every platform, only while the conversation in view runs
a shell call in the foreground. Stop is on a background row and in the Agent
map, with Stop all there. On the Model API backend a moved call answers the
model at once, and what it printed is added to the replay as a user note that
waits for the next request, because this backend makes no model call nobody
asked for. `!` commands run as typed, outside any turn, with no approval card
in any permission mode, and never in Restricted Mode; on the Model API backend
they run until they finish or the person stops them. Explain sends the whole selection.
Full record: [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D41 — One memory for both backends (M49, 2026-09-25)

Memory is one store with two users: `src/core/memory/memoryStore.ts` places,
validates, reads and writes notes by Muse Code's rules, and a note written on
one backend is read on the other. The Model API memory tools are Muse Code's
and are offered in a trusted workspace only. Approval is like an edit, not
like Muse Code: a write asks in Manual, runs in Auto and Edit automatically,
and is refused in Plan, and a read never asks. The extension keeps the index
true: a note the Model API tool or the Memory view creates gets its line in
its scope's `MEMORY.md`. A path through any link below the workspace or
data-home anchor is refused. Without proven interoperation, the extension does
not take or imitate Muse Code's lock. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D42 — MCP servers on the Model API backend (2026-09-25)

The Model API backend runs the MCP servers Muse Code would, with a client of
its own and no new dependency. There is one set per window: the servers belong
to the Model API host, and nothing starts in Restricted Mode. A required
server that is not running fails the turn with the reason and the fix. On
Windows, if the M50 job executable cannot be compiled or started, stdio fails
closed instead of starting without containment. An MCP tool is arbitrary code:
it runs in Bypass, asks in Auto, Manual and Edit automatically and is refused
in Plan, while a tool its server marks read-only runs in Auto and asks in
Plan. Resources, prompts, sampling, roots and elicitation are not done. Full
record: [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D43 — Enterprise network and posture (2026-09-25)

The extension has no proxy client of its own, because VS Code's is complete
and follows the user's VS Code settings. Wherever Muse Code's environment
names a proxy, `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` and `::1` are added to its `NO_PROXY`,
and a malformed `http.proxy` or `http.noProxy` falls back to an empty value
instead of becoming a process environment variable. Certificates for Muse Code
are left to the system store, so the extension never sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`.
`museSpark.sandboxNetwork` is machine-scoped, and `--no-session-log` is not
offered. `prompt_cache_retention` is `in_memory` by default, with `24h` only
when the user chooses it. As amended on 2026-09-27, VS Code patches
`WebSocket` only from 1.112.0, so on 1.101 to 1.111 Muse Voice's socket goes
to Meta without VS Code's proxy and certificate handling; while `http.proxy`
is set there the microphone stays unavailable with the reason instead of
recording audio that cannot be sent (MSM56, 2026-10-17). Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D45 — Subagents on both backends (M48, 2026-09-25)

The Model API backend runs bounded child sessions with their own conversation
and the parent's workspace rules, tool permissions and model. M48 requires a
machine-scoped gate, price acceptance, one-use consent and a four-request
ceiling for every new child task, including retries. Every new child task,
whether spawn, follow-up, reopen or resume, requires a one-use approval in
every mode, Bypass included, and Plan refuses it. The ceiling is four actual
Model API response POST attempts for that task, which HTTP and whole-stream
retries and tool rounds also spend, and no grant survives a process restart.
The child cannot spawn further children or ask the user directly, and its
token usage counts once in the parent's total. On Muse Code, `subagent/reopen`
and `subagent/readResult` remain unavailable until a bounded live
owner-command capture establishes their success shapes. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D46 — Conversation rewind and side chat (2026-09-25)

Conversation rewind uses the `session/fork` cut point before the selected user
turn, then restores that turn's prompt as a draft; the first turn rewinds to a
fresh conversation. A steered user card's fork cut must use the preceding
distinct completed turn or a fresh conversation, and rewind of a selected turn
still running is hidden and refused until its steered image replay settles. A
Model API fork rejects a cut before its latest compaction summary. Side chat
opens a separate tab forked from completed turns, with Plan mode forced and
the inherited goal cleared; the Model API backend denies write tools in that
mode. On Muse Code 1.3.0 on Windows both conversation actions remain
unavailable until the CLI fixes `session/fork`. Image restoration never treats
a webview-supplied ID as a durable backend ID. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D47 — File input follows each backend's proven wire (2026-09-25)

File input follows each backend's proven wire, and no invented part is sent to
Muse Code. On the Model API, PDF bytes, checked by header, may be attached
from the file picker, clipboard or drop, up to 32 MB each, and a bounded UTF-8
text file picked from the trusted workspace becomes a named `input_text` part.
On Muse Code, a PDF attachment gets a clear refusal naming the Model API
backend, and a bounded text attachment becomes an MSP text part. Attached
images and countable PDF page images share 50 slots per new message, and an
uncountable PDF reserves all 50. The Model API extension also caps base64
media to 48 million characters per new message and replay request, and its
replay keeps the newest visible media within both budgets, replacing older
media with a plain explanation. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D48 — A popup before every paid use (M58, 2026-09-27)

**CM352 owner update (2026-10-11).** Extension Muse Voice asks once before the
first charge with its hourly list price and the shared daily budget. Allow once
covers this window; Always covers the workspace until revoked. Each recording
still passes the paid gate and budget/account/context admission and shows a
loud duration/cost estimate. This replaces the per-recording popup policy for
the extension microphone; ACP/headless availability and consent stay unchanged.

The owner (2026-09-27): "anything requiring extra payment should promt you
with a popup that asks allow once allow always in this workspace or deny".
Until then the paid features asked in four different ways: an in-chat card
with Allow once and Reject for a Model API image or child task, a native
dialog for an image on Muse Code, a scheduled run and a child task started
from the Agent map, and nothing per use for web search and Muse Voice (D34:
the price accepted once, then only the row, the badge and the tally).

- **One popup, three answers.** `PaidUseConsent.allows`
  (`src/core/paid/paidConsent.ts`) asks through `askPaidUse`
  (`src/host/paid/paidHost.ts`), a native modal naming what is about to be
  billed and its price, with **Allow once**, **Allow always in this
  workspace** and **Deny**; closing it is Deny. It asks in every permission
  mode, Bypass included. A paid call never gets an approval card or a
  session rule any more: `paidChoices`, the `paidTool` subject and the
  card's price line are gone.
- **What asks, and when.** An image, before it is bought (after every check
  that can refuse it for free, as before). A child task, before its grant;
  Plan still refuses it. A scheduled run, before its turn. A Muse Voice
  recording, before the recorder starts; a stop pressed while the popup is
  open cancels the start. Web search, once per prompt before its first
  request: Meta runs the searches inside the response and the model decides
  whether to search, so no popup can come before each search; Deny sends
  that prompt without the `web_search` tool. A child task searches only
  when its parent's prompt was allowed to (its grant carries the answer), or,
  for a task the user starts from the Agent map, when web search is allowed
  always here. A child never asks for itself.
- **"Always" is per workspace, and revocable.** It is kept in the
  workspace's own state (feature names with a grant generation, no content),
  offered and honoured only in a trusted workspace with a folder open. Every
  change to a feature's price acceptance (turned off, or a new price
  accepted) counts its generation up in global state, which voids every
  workspace's "always" for it. **Ask again every time** in Account & usage
  clears them for this workspace.
- **Still loud when silent.** A use that no longer asks keeps its paid row,
  the badge (whose tooltip names the features allowed always), and the tally;
  Account & usage marks each such feature "on, allowed always in this
  workspace". A hook's `allow` never answers the popup; a hook that demands
  a question, and a paid image aimed at a protected path (D24), ask even when
  the feature is allowed always.
- **Not asked:** an ordinary Model API turn the user types. Choosing the
  Model API backend with a pay-as-you-go key is that consent (D1, D37); the
  popup covers what costs extra beyond it.

**M80 headless amendment (D65):** interactive consent above is unchanged.
Headless images use the explicit flag, `acceptEdits`, hard cap and per-use
admission/tally; no remembered grant is accessed. Hosted search is refused.

### D49 — Coding quality first: what to build next (2026-09-27)

Coding quality first: the ranking rule (what most improves the code the user
gets comes first — the model seeing its edits' effects, understanding the
code, reading the pages it needs; then reviewing and shipping, fewer tokens on
long tasks, more agents safely, connectivity; both-backends-first within a
wave), the carried rules (model calls beyond the user's own turn are billed,
opt in, priced and ask first; Restricted Mode runs no git or shell;
token/quality trades ship only after M75's paired evaluation holds the floors;
one-token ide-server tool constraints), and the M67–M85 wave batch it ordered
(all shipped). Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

- "research the claude code harness and any upcoming features … and also
  https://github.com/NVlabs/SoL-Pi and see if there are gaps between our
  product and theirs that we can fill to make our product compete with the
  claudes, and the codexes, and the open codes, and open claws, the t3
  codes …"
- "we are geared towards coding so thats where our focus should be the
  strongest, but anything that could help productivity and connectivity
  and compatibility thats fine, and maybe some of this helps on the cli
  side as well"
- Then: "put together the list of improvements you think will be the
  best for this project for our users to get the highest quality and
  value then add them to the plan".

The research is in `docs/research/competitive-landscape-2026-09.md`: public
sources, no sign-in, no spend. It found the extension at or near parity
with Claude Code on:

- subagents, hooks, MCP, skills, goals, scheduled prompts;
- rewind, side chat, worktrees, memory, compaction;
- permission modes and plan mode.

It is ahead of most of the field on paid-use consent, languages,
accessibility and machine-scoped settings. It is behind on the loop that
makes an agent's code correct, and on the workflow around a change.

**The ranking rule.** What most improves the code a user gets comes
first: the model seeing the effects of its edits, understanding the code
it changes, and reading the pages it needs. Next comes reviewing and
shipping that code, then spending fewer tokens on long tasks, then
running more agents safely, then connectivity. Within a wave, what serves
both backends comes before what serves one.

**The two backends.**

- **Model API:** the extension owns the loop, so every item below can be
  built in full.
- **Muse Code:** MSP bounds what the backend can do. Two routes still
  reach it:
  - the extension's `ide` MCP server, which every Muse Code session
    already loads (M5, M44), can offer the new tools (code intelligence,
    web fetch, the browser check);
  - everything that lives in the extension serves both backends: review,
    git, checkpoints, the session board, notifications.
- What neither route can reach is named in its milestone and, where it
  matters, asked of Meta upstream: tool-output projection, fused edit and
  verify, `web_fetch` enablement.

**Rules carried.**

- **Paid calls.** An item that makes model calls beyond the user's own
  turn is billed to the key. Such items are opt in, priced, and ask before
  each use (D30, D48). They are:
  - the Auto reviewer;
  - the second-opinion and reviewer agents, run on their own or as a
    child (D45);
  - the log reducer (M73);
  - best-of-N attempts, on the Model API only.
- **The user's own turn** is the model calls made while answering a message
  or command the user sent, in that conversation: a compaction or a
  follow-up the harness adds on the way is part of it, as is a
  `/review`, commit message or PR body the user asks for. Calls started
  without one (a schedule, a wake, an automatic review, a child or
  reviewer run on its own) are beyond it, as M52 set for scheduled
  prompts. Nothing generates text on its own.
- **Restricted Mode** runs no git and no shell (D13, D24). A milestone that
  needs them is unavailable there and says why.
- **Measured first.** A harness change that trades tokens against
  quality (M73, M74) ships only after M75's paired evaluation shows the
  capability floors held on muse-spark. M75 is therefore built first in
  wave 3, and M73 and M74 each land together with their own passing run:
  until that run passes, the mechanism has no setting and no code path a
  user can reach.
- **Tools on the `ide` server.** It is one endpoint for the whole
  window, with one token and no session identity, and it is attached even
  in Restricted Mode, so it cannot see a Muse Code session's permission
  mode. A tool served there that writes, runs a command or reaches the
  network therefore:
  - is not listed while the workspace is untrusted, and a network tool is
    not listed while `museSpark.sandboxNetwork` denies the network;
  - declares its MCP annotations (`readOnlyHint: false`, and
    `openWorldHint: true` for the network); a read-only tool declares
    `readOnlyHint: true`;
  - confirms each call in the extension's own modal, as the image tools
    do (M44).
- **Untrusted content.** Fetched pages, PR and review comments, imported
  files and tool output are data, never instructions. They are marked as
  untrusted where the model receives them, and nothing in them can raise
  a permission, pick a model or skip a question. A conversation built on
  such content (an imported session, a PR someone else wrote, a plan file
  picked from Plans… in M79) starts in a mode that asks, whatever
  `museSpark.initialPermissionMode` says, and only the user's own action
  relaxes it.
- **Automatic actions follow the mode.** Anything the extension runs on
  its own (checks after an edit, a memory flush, a review turn) takes the
  same path as the call it stands for: a shell command asks wherever the
  shell tool would, a memory write where a memory write would, and Plan
  and Restricted Mode refuse what they refuse today.
- **Captured wire.** Wire shapes come from live captures (AGENTS.md
  rule 13).
- **Ported code.** Code ported from SoL-Pi (MIT) keeps NVIDIA's notice in
  `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` and the file headers. That file is generated
  from `node_modules` licences by `scripts/third-party-notices.mjs`, so
  the first milestone that ports code (M68 or M73) adds a list of ported
  sources to the generator, which its staleness check then covers (with a
  drill).

**The program**, in order. Size S is two days or less, M is three to five
days, L is one to two weeks. The milestone numbers were given before the
order was settled, so the table, not the numbers, is the order: M80 comes
after wave 5's others because it waits for PR #32, and D50's M85 comes
last, after M73, M75, M76 and M78 that it builds on, and after the
owner's TypeSafe key for its capture.

| Wave                       | Milestone | What                                                                                                                                       | Backends                              | Who has it                              | Size |
| -------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---- |

**Not taken.**

- A hosted relay, mobile apps, and chat-app control (T3 Connect, OpenClaw
  channels). These are not coding-first, and Remote Control waits on Meta
  (sdk #36).
- Model routing across vendors (Crush, OpenCode). The extension is
  Meta-only by design (D1). D50's TypeSafe assist is not a coding model
  and never answers; it is the one non-Meta model call, experimental and
  off by default.
- GitLab and other forges. VS Code ships no built-in authentication for
  them, so M71 is GitHub only.
- A plugin marketplace of our own. M83 imports others' formats instead,
  and Muse Code's own plugins keep working.

### D50 — TypeSafe, experimental: an assist to the Muse model, never a replacement (2026-09-27)

TypeSafe may only assist the Muse model: it never answers the user, writes
code, or decides an action alone, and where a signal is missing or unsure,
behaviour is exactly what it is without TypeSafe. A "safe" score never skips a
question and never becomes an allow on its own. As amended on 2026-10-04 by
D77, TypeSafe is one engine of the Muse Judge and no longer a feature of its
own, and the setting is `museSpark.judge.*`. The original "off by default" is
superseded: the judge's default is `auto`, and a paid source asks once before
its first charge. Every remote engine, TypeSafe included, stays off while
`museSpark.confidentialWorkspace` is on. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D51 — Turn checkpoints live in a shadow repository (M72, amended by M86)

Turn checkpoints live in a shadow repository in the extension's own storage,
and nothing is written or refreshed in the workspace's `.git`. As amended by
M86, restoration is narrowed to the model's own file-tool writes: a file is
restored only along an unbroken chain of recorded before/after bytes ending in
exactly what is on disk now, or is counted unchanged when it is already at the
earlier state. Commands, hooks, MCP tools, the user's edits and other windows'
writes are never undone. Each model file-tool publication is recorded in a
fsynced per-instance journal before conditional publication. File restoration
requires an attached Model API session and confirmed process safety, and is
refused while any turn runs. In Restricted Mode the extension runs no
checkpoint git and records no new writes. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D60 — Muse Spark Code beyond VS Code: the IDE compatibility program (2026-09-26)

The IDE compatibility program, kept whole in `docs/ide-compatibility.md`,
makes one product in four families: the VS Code extension qualified in the
editors built on VS Code, one agent over the Agent Client Protocol, native
plugins that embed the React panel, and a terminal or adjacent interface. The
engine and the UI are shared and the host is an adapter; VS Code stays the
reference client, and its behaviour does not change while boundaries move. In
every adapter the key never reaches a child process, a launch argument, an
environment variable, a webview message or a general IPC field, an adapter
whose client cannot show the price and ask first offers no paid feature, and
Muse's approval policy is never loosened because a protocol allows it. Support
is measured per host. Nothing is installed or billed unasked. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D61 — The Model API key outside VS Code (2026-09-26)

Inside VS Code the key stays in SecretStorage. An agent that runs with no VS
Code keeps it in the operating system's credential store, reached in-process
through `@napi-rs/keyring`, with Linux pinned to the Secret Service; there is
no plaintext fallback. There is one entry per user, service `Muse Spark Code
(Unofficial)` and account `museSpark.modelApiKey`, shared by every editor that
runs the agent. `muse-spark-code-acp auth set` reads the key from the terminal
with echo off. The key never goes into an argument, an environment variable, a
file, a log, an ACP message or a child process. The agent takes `META_API_KEY`
and every other credential variable out of its own environment and hands them
back to Muse Code's processes only. CI does not use `auth set`, a throwaway
keyring or an environment-key fallback. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D62 — The ACP agent, and the order the editors come in (2026-09-26)

One executable, `muse-spark-code-acp`, speaks ACP v1 on stdio and runs the
panel's engine, not a second one. The backend is chosen at launch, `--backend
museCode` (the default) or `--backend modelApi`, and there is no "auto".
Nothing runs by a translation default: a permission request the client
cancels, or answers with an option it was not offered, is decided with the
backend's deny choice. A folder's rules, skills and memory load only with
`--trust-workspace`. As amended on 2026-09-27, every paid use asks in the
editor, and headless `exec` replaces editor questions with denials. The
most-used editors come first: VS Code's family through the `.vsix` and Open
VSX (M62), then the editors reached through this agent (M63), then M64, M65
and the constrained hosts (M66). Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D64 — Exposure-preserving import, replacing credential detection (2026-10-02)

Five independent review rounds found spellings that bypassed credential
detection. M83 now controls destinations instead of inspecting content.
Personal files stay personal; a git-ignored project source goes only to an
ignored project target or a personal target; a tracked project source may
go to any of those places. A non-repository folder counts as tracked.
Canonical path checks and the safe metadata git runner classify sources;
targets are classified again after final path checks at publication or
editor edit time. Unknown classification refuses the item.

Five independent review rounds found spellings that bypassed credential
detection. M83 owns destinations instead of inspecting content: the preview
lists kind, source item name, scope and target path, never values. Full
record: [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

Readiness: the lead's M83x brief and REDESIGN-EXPOSURE.md settle scope and
all ten RV83e findings. Reuse the scanner, native editor, path guards,
exclusive publication and safe git metadata options. No dependency,
detector, heuristic, option or plan-format migration. The delivery ledger
validator remains deferred because this canonical plan has no ledger;
focused behavioral evidence and SHA-256-restored red drills go in
`docs/certification/m83e.md`. Full quality and native UI remain lead-owned.

### D65 — Headless execution and CI key readers (M80, 2026-10-02)

Numbered D64 while it was built; M83 merged its own D64 first, so this
decision became D65 at integration (2026-10-02).

**The exception: headless runs in CI (M80, PLAN D65).** GitHub supplies the Model API key to the Action's own run-step process through its environment. The step directly execs the trusted launcher, which deletes that variable before it starts any child and holds the key only in memory until final cleanup. It sends the key only over private standard input to two trusted installed agent commands: `muse-spark-code-acp exec --key-stdin` for the run, and `muse-spark-code-acp scan-secrets --key-stdin` for the exact private staged patch. Both hold it in memory only, clear their references in finally, and never store it. No Git, tool, hook, check, install, apply or other child receives it in an environment, argument or file. The launcher's initial OS environment can remain inspectable by the same user; deleting the variable does not erase that record or guarantee memory zeroization. Nothing else is excepted.

**Other-CI transport (CM80CI-R4, 2026-10-10).** The bootstrap shell never
reads/copies the value or creates a key file. Its download subshell unsets
names/aliases from the launcher's generated list; its parent execs Node with
the original vendor environment. Node takes the vendor source first (GitLab
File variable is read directly, never copied), refuses conflicting names,
strips names and values before children and keeps the credential only in
memory for private stdin and redaction. This replaces R2's environment
handoff and R3's private key transport file. Vendor-managed secret-file
creation and automatic phases remain vendor boundaries, not launcher
children; their qualification limits are explicit in M80's record.

**CM80CIR6 review repair (2026-10-10, RVCM80CI5).** Remove Azure's
pipeline start-time expression and reader entirely: admission uses the
bootstrap's measured epoch time with a fixed 10-minute pre-bootstrap setup
allowance. This allowance covers job initialization, full-history checkout
and UseNode on a qualified runner; it is a required worst-case setup bound,
not a universal Azure guarantee. The Azure job becomes 45 minutes so its
20-minute turn, measured bootstrap, 10-minute setup reserve and all launcher
tails fit. Hosted qualification must prove setup stays within 10 minutes;
runners that cannot meet that bound must not use this template. No organization
timezone or vendor date expression participates in admission. Parent bootstrap
holders and cleanup copies use the reserved `muse_ci_internal_` prefix;
declared aliases using that prefix or the bootstrap configuration prefixes
`MUSE_CI_`, `MUSE_INPUT_`, `MUSE_AGENT_` refuse before download and in Node,
covering the temp/start/package transport bindings assigned at exec. Tests
check the prefix against the generated unset list,
exercise ordinary aliases matching every old holder, and prove missing-exec
cleanup under sh, dash and bash with unsetting applied. Azure's final template
test rejects vendor time expressions, including malformed ones. Every finding
gets a regression and a byte-exact red drill in `docs/certification/cm80ci.md`.
No new dependency, wider guard, paid/live call or hosted-support claim.

Local OS-store authentication is unchanged. Stdin CI uses neither `auth set`
nor a throwaway keyring nor an environment-key fallback inside the agent.
One bounded launcher owns diff generation, exec, extraction, patch Git,
the trusted scanner and publication. Cancellation closes publication, stops
later children and clears key references in finally; it cannot guarantee
physical memory zeroization or graceful Windows signal delivery.

Headless paid images require an explicit flag, `acceptEdits`, a hard USD cap
and per-use ledger admission/settlement. Protected paths and `requiresAsking`
are denied. No remembered grants, ordinary approval grants or translated-title
policy decisions apply. Hosted search, voice, subagents and schedules stay off;
the subscription pays none of these Model API calls. D48/D62's interactive
popup policy remains in force for interactive sessions.

Admission reserves conservative request input and the resolved output cap for
each attempt, including retries, with integer micro-USD upward rounding (EXECPROV,
2026-10-11). There is no fixed full-context startup minimum. Each request is
capped at the model's own output limit (0.18.0 policy cap, kept at the merge
2026-10-12); the cap feeds the body, request schema, ledger shape check and
first real reservation. Lost receipts keep their request reservation. Configured
price cards include their captured cache-write premiums and long-context tier.
Request admission uses the canonical-body UTF-8 bound where no verified exact
count is available; Anthropic reserves its estimate plus 25%, capped by that
size bound. Only the final estimate error can exceed the cap: the full actual
cost is retained and another request stops (LEDGER, 2026-10-12). Initial HTTP
refusals before generation settle at zero; cancellation without final usage
retains unresolved liability separately from confirmed spend. See
`docs/certification/exec-provider.md`; full aggregate quality and installed/live
certification remain lead-owned.
Configured defaults are authoritative in exec and ACP; no missing default selects
another model. Ephemeral exec omits durable usage history and reports
usageHistory=omitted_ephemeral. Command --help stays local; help reference opens
the complete catalogue (EXECPROV, 2026-10-11). The usage panel shares the portable
journal through runtimeAccounting, installing the caller’s language before use,
to retain its existing size cap.

Proposals, secret-free tests and reviewer-approved push run in separate jobs.
Text patches publish only after exact staged-byte scanning. Any binary/image
change withholds the entire patch. Registry installs require npm 11.19.0's
verified provenance bundle, subject/digest and release-workflow certificate
identity; unsigned candidate digests provide a different claim.

### D66 — Panel polish from the owner's requests of 2026-10-03 (M87)

D66 records the choices made for the owner's panel requests of 2026-10-03: M87

### D67 — Saved prompts, bookmarks and timed sends (M88)

D67 covers saved prompts, prompt sequences, bookmarks, timed sends and Resume
after a limit, and two of its parts are superseded. Saved prompts belong to
the panel, not to skills; their storage is superseded by D98 (M118), where the
library is built, while the caps, damage rule and sync opt-in carry over, and
sync through `museSpark.syncPromptsAndBookmarks` is off by default and
machine-scoped. In a prompt sequence each later step is sent only when the
previous turn ends `completed` and no other turn is queued. A bookmarked Model
API session is not deleted by `museSpark.cleanupPeriodDays`. Timed sends (item 15)
and Resume after a limit (item 16) are superseded by D95 (M115), where they
run unattended under a schedule's grant instead of in the conversation's mode;
the rest of D67 stands. Full record:
