### D123 — The provider judges a key; no key is refused for its shape (lane PROVKEYS, 2026-10-12; numbered D108 until the 2026-10-17 merge with main, where D108 is the test overhaul)

No key is ever refused for its looks, on any surface. What decides is the
provider's own answer to the first authenticated request the product already
makes (the free model-list key test); a refusal shows the provider's reason.
The only checks before sending are the ones that protect the person and hold
for every provider — the value is not empty, has no whitespace or line break
inside, and is not obviously the wrong thing (a URL, a file path, placeholder
text) — each asked as a "use it anyway?" question, never a dead end. This
supersedes M95 lane K's "password box with the preset's live shape check": the
box accepts any non-blank key, and no preset carries a key-shape field at
all — the provider judges every key through the free key test, while each
preset's hint names where the key comes from. Where the person can answer
(the panel's modal, a terminal prompt), the "use it anyway?" question waits
for the answer and a "no" asks for the key again; where nothing can answer
(piped stdin), the run continues to the provider. The endpoint
policy, log redaction and the product's own Meta-key format are unchanged.
Full record: [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D204 — Claimed-shipped milestones: an `@unwired` tag is resolved by the user-visible promise (MSM58M69, 2026-10-17)

A verification scan found `@unwired` tags carrying shipped milestone ids
(M58, M69). The tag alone does not mean the promise is broken: TESTCUT
tagged every unused export with its nearest shipped id. Each item is
resolved against the plan's user-visible promise, not against the tag:

- **Promise already kept through another path:** the dead export is
  removed, not wired. M69's `htmlToMarkdown` had no callers (a prior
  dead-code lane verified zero references; the revert restored it only
  incidentally): both backends convert through `convertHtmlJob` on the
  page worker. Wiring a second conversion path would duplicate behaviour
  to satisfy the gate.
- **Designed for a milestone that is still building:** it stays unwired
  and no other lane wires it. `askSchedulePaidConsent` and
  `createSchedulePaidScope` are M115 Lane U's region
  (`src/core/paid/paidConsent.ts`, the schedule scope); `paidAccountQuestion`
  and `AccountPaidUseConsent` are M108 lane P's per-account consent. The
  tag keeps knip honest until their lanes land.
- **Fail-closed meanwhile, at the sites a person can reach:** a paid V2
  draft is refused unless the trusted caller carries `scheduledPrompts`
  and a budget at least its cap (`src/runtime/schedules/surface.ts`,
  again in `control.ts`); the panel's caller carries neither
  (`runtime.ts`, `scheduledPrompts: false`), and the editor's default
  draft cap is 0 (`schedulesBridge.ts`). A CLI/ACP caller with the flag
  and budget can create a paid draft today, but it cannot spend: no
  production code constructs `createSchedulePaidScope` or calls
  `reserveSchedule`, `UnattendedRun` is never constructed, and the one
  `ScheduleDelivery` composition (`engine.ts`) has no session target
  (`find` returns nothing, `open`/`fresh`/`runs` throw
  target-unavailable). Lane U therefore wires creation consent, the run
  scope and the reservation **before** any delivery target; nothing here
  claims a firing V2 run checks consent today (corrected by RVMSM58M69,
  which also added the surface-refusal tests to
  `test/unit/schedulePaidConsent.test.ts`; that file's helper tests prove
  only the unwired helpers' own logic).
- **Refusals stay default-off:** web fetch keeps refusing private/local
  addresses and credentialed URLs. A per-role permission for the person's
  own network is NOT FIXED and not built (owner's choice of 2026-10-16
  allows one in the model role settings, which have no web-fetch entry
  today); when it is built, the refuse sites are `checkPageUrl`
  (`src/core/web/pageUrl.ts`), `isPublicAddress`
  (`src/core/web/publicAddress.ts`) and the pin in
  `src/core/web/webFetch.ts`, and every caller (VS Code, ACP/headless,
  both backends) must pass the role's answer through. MSM58M69 shipped
  no behaviour change for it.

### D109 — Model-call turn limits preserve the answer (TOOLROUNDS, 2026-10-11; renumbered from D108 at merge, main took D108 for the test overhaul)

The Model API turn cap is a limit, not a loop detector: no round count of ours
ends a turn (2026-10-17, D121/D208: the 200-call default no longer exists;
ordinary reviews and coding jobs need more than fifty calls, and only a
provider's documented limit or a value the person set may stop anything).
A caller allowance bounds the run — exec's `--max-requests`, a best-of-N
attempt ceiling, or another caller bound — and an existing caller request cap
is read with its remaining allowance. Reserve the last permitted call for a
tools-disabled wrap-up; retain its answer and report a translated, typed
request-limit stop in every host. Person-set money caps, compaction accounting
and queued-input promotion remain in force. Certification: [toolrounds](docs/certification/toolrounds.md).

### D208 — No spending check without a limit the person set (spend-simple, owner 2026-10-17; numbered D121 until the 0.19.0 join, when that number was found shared with D121 limits-only-on-models)

The owner, verbatim: "why are there spending checks each call this seems
like not the right way to do it make sure you research properly. whatever
get the app to pruduction faster with no bugs. i dont care about the
credits if the app is proven working." With the standing rule of the same
day (only the providers' limits are hard-coded; every other limit is the
person's, none by default), this supersedes the LEDGER design (§3, §6, §7):
the atomic claim journal, its cross-process admission lock, the 100 ms
admission bound and its benchmark.

- **No limit set, no check.** With no session budget, no editor
  `museSpark.paidDailyBudgetUsd` and no agent `paidDailyBudgetUsd` (all
  none by default, no maximum of ours), nothing is reserved, locked or
  written, and no spend record is read, before a send; only the settings
  that would hold a limit are read. Each reply's own usage line still shows
  its cost.
- **A limit the person set keeps a running total.** The session budget's
  total lives in the session that owns it, grows after each call from the
  usage the provider reported, and is saved with the session, so a resume
  continues from it. A daily budget's total is lock-free: each process adds
  to its own file in the day's folder, and a read sums the files.
- **Stop before, in plain words.** A request whose estimate (its input plus
  the model's floor output, search fees included) would pass the limit is
  not sent; the stop names the estimate, the limit and what was used, and
  the daily stop names the setting. One warning comes when what is left no
  longer fits a request like the last one. A reply may cost more than its
  estimate; the next request is then the one stopped.
- **A reservation is never spend.** A response that ended without its usage
  counts as cost unknown, with what is known, and adds nothing to the total.
- **A refusal books nothing.** A request the provider refused before
  generating anything (`NON_BILLABLE_HTTP_REJECTIONS`) is withdrawn from the
  run ledger with its request count and adds nothing to any total, even when
  a provider adapter rethrows the error without its status: the transport
  tells the attempt guard first (`onRefused`).
- **Kept as they were:** the exec run ledger's own rules otherwise
  (`--max-budget-usd`, its published v2 schema), the Tab ledger, the team
  meter and account thresholds. Record, the $120.00 origin and every removal:
  `docs/certification/spend-simple.md`.

### D209 — One .vsix per platform, each within the unchanged budget (lane VSIXPLATFORM, 2026-10-18; numbered D123 until the 0.19.0 join, when that number was found shared)

The universal .vsix carries every platform's native helpers and is near
its 3,788,800-byte budget (D6) with 131 KB of open pull requests and
4.7 MB of vault keyring binaries still to come. The budget is never
raised and no feature is cut, so the release ships one package per
supported target instead: win32-x64, win32-arm64, darwin-x64,
darwin-arm64, linux-x64 and linux-arm64 (`vsce package --target`, locked
vsce 4.0.0; engines.vscode `^1.99.0` clears the ≥1.61 platform-extension
floor). Each target carries only its own platform's native pieces plus
the platform-neutral bundles; `native/runner/*` ships everywhere because
the SSH runner copies the helper to the remote side. Windows targets
carry the same arch-independent sources (the .ps1 run directly, the .cs
compiled on the person's machine), so win32-arm64 is supported today.
Each darwin target ships only its own architecture's thin slices
(amended 2026-10-20, VSIXDARWIN): darwin-arm64 carries the arm64 .app, vault
and peer, darwin-x64 the x64 ones, each signed and verified the same way
(build.sh signs and version-checks both; execution probes run on the host
arch). The split saves ~129 KB per darwin package at 0.19.0 (measured on
macmini), which the unchanged budget needs alongside the webview/skill
archive savings; the ACP universal package carries both architectures and
the runtime selects by architecture, as it already does for the Linux
helpers. The universal sentence above stood while the webview dominated;
the 0.19.0 measurements showed the darwin targets still ~92 KB over after
the single-copy change, so per-arch ships.
Beside the six, the release ships the untargeted universal package (no
`--target`): VS Code serves it as the fallback on every platform without
its own package, so Alpine (`alpine-x64`, `alpine-arm64`) and `linux-armhf`
servers — `extensionKind: ["workspace"]`, so a Dev Container or Remote SSH
window installs the extension on the server — keep installing exactly what
they ran before. (There is no `web` target to serve: the extension has no
`browser` entry, so VS Code never installs it on web.) Every one of the
seven packages is checked against the same D6 budget; CI builds and checks
all seven, and the release publishes all seven to the Marketplace and Open
VSX: every artifact is published before any visibility poll runs, all share
one 30-minute poll deadline inside 60-minute jobs, and unfinished targets
are re-checked in the same job, so a cancelled job never leaves only some
targets published.

VSIXFIT C (2026-10-20): the fallback stopped carrying every platform's helpers — the full universal measured 4,443,930 bytes and cannot meet the unchanged budget. It now carries the platform-neutral content plus the Linux helpers only (`native/linux/x64/*`, `native/linux/arm64/*`, `native/runner/*`), never the darwin or Windows pieces: VS Code never serves the fallback where a targeted package exists, so it only ever reaches Linux-family platforms, and that is exactly what those servers ran before. Measured on the linuxlt rig: the linux-x64 target passes the 3,788,800-byte gate with headroom and the fallback is estimated to pass with thin headroom (see `docs/certification/vsix-platform.md` §2); darwin stages pack helperless locally with the CI binaries estimated on top, and the complete win32 stages fail the gate by 12 KB, all confirmed by CI.

VSIXWEB (2026-10-20): with no lever left inside "budget never raised, nothing cut", the two biggest loose crowds pack solid instead — `dist/webview/**` as one brotli-11 `dist/webview.json.br` (190 members, extracted and SHA-256-verified into global storage on first use) and the vendored skill as one brotli-11 beside its loose `LICENSE`+`VENDOR.json` — saving ~181 KB per target with no feature, locale, text or helper cut, bringing win32-x64 back inside the unchanged budget (see `docs/certification/vsix-platform.md` §2).
Evidence: `docs/certification/vsix-platform.md`.

Amended 2026-10-24 (CC-INT1, the owner: "Move budget to measured +15%"): the
budget every one of the seven packages meets is now 4800 KiB (4,915,200
bytes), measured win32-x64 4,273,804 bytes +15%, rounded up to 25 KiB (D6,
VSIXBUDGET). The shape stays: one package per platform, each checked against
the same budget.

### D210 — One package per platform target (lane RUTRUTHL2, 2026-10-18; numbered D123 until the 0.19.0 join, when that number was found shared)

The universal `.vsix` and universal ACP tarball each demand every
platform's native helpers, so neither packs on a single-OS checkout:
a Linux lane cannot build the arm64 helper's cross toolchain or any
macOS helper. The packagers take `--target <platform>-<arch>` (the six
desktop targets VS Code runs on); a targeted package stages only its
own platform's native pieces (`native/runner/*` ships everywhere
because the SSH runner copies the helper to the remote side) and names
its target in its filename, while the universal package keeps all.
Every target is checked against the same unchanged D6 budget. CI and
release publication of per-target artifacts stay with the release
packaging lane; this decision covers the packager mechanism and the
local proof (`muse-spark-code-linux-x64-0.19.0.vsix` and
`muse-spark-code-acp-0.19.0-linux-x64.tgz` packed and inventoried on
`linuxlt`).

### D211 — Manual asks the person on Muse Code 1.4.7: the `:ask-me` profile (lane MANUALMODE, 2026-10-18; numbered D123 until the 0.19.0 join, when that number was found shared)

Real use on Muse Code 1.4.7 showed Manual running commands with no approval
reaching the editor: the session files record `"policy_decision":
"allow:llm_judge"`. MSP `promptUnmatched` does not remove Muse Code's LLM
judge; neither do `muse serve` flags (it refuses `--approval-judge`) nor the
MSP modes (closed enum, select-never-create). Muse Code 1.4.7's stable
`session/start.permissionProfile` (amendment 42624) does: `:ask-me` keeps
the session's access and selects the human reviewer, while the default
`:auto-review` lets the judge allow eligible actions. So interactive Manual
and Edit-automatically sessions start with `:ask-me`, Auto sessions with
`:auto-review`, and every mode switch re-syncs the profile (experimental
`session/setPermissionProfile`, tolerated as `methodNotFound` on older
hosts). Headless ACP starts (exec and every other non-interactive path)
pass no profile and behave as before; a mode switch whose profile step
fails with anything else puts the previous approval mode back before
throwing, so the menu never shows a mode the host is not running; and a
scheduled admission on a Manual conversation runs with `:auto-review` while
the unattended run is in charge, putting the conversation's reviewer back
when the mode is restored. The failure paths are closed too (lane
PR251FIX2, 2026-10-19; corrected by lane PR251FIX3B after Grok's second
re-review GRV251D): resume, fork and load seed the handle from the
approval mode the envelope serves, so the first mode change rolls back
like a live one. Every mode-switch failure names the wire mode the host
runs: a refused mode command, or a profile step the rollback undoes,
throws `ModeKeptError` with the running mode and turns stay live; an
unknown previous mode, a failed rollback, a torn adoption, or a failed
schedule restore quarantines with `PermissionReviewerError` naming the
running mode instead. A refused command releases its effect without
forgetting the mode, so later turns and mode changes are judged on their
own. The Modes menu (panel composer) and the editor (ACP) show the running
mode (`composerModeForApprovalMode`) with the error's own sentence; when no
menu mode selects it, the panel refuses the send in flight instead (lane
PR251FIX4, 2026-10-20, after Grok's third re-review GRV251E: a torn forward
change says the named mode runs without its reviewer installed; a torn
rollback says the previous mode is restored with its reviewer still
installed, with turns refused until the mode is set again; a refused
schedule restore quarantines too, naming the mode the host still runs; a
quarantine keeps its sentence, which the next refused turn repeats; lane
PR251FIX5, 2026-10-19, after Grok's fourth re-review GRV251F: the rollback
notice naming the recorded mode keeps that sentence, and a genuinely
different mode replaces it with the sentence naming that mode
(`permissionModeChangedWhileQuarantined`: new turns stay refused until the
mode is set again, with no reviewer or tear words, since the notice
installs and removes no reviewer — lane PR251FIX6, 2026-10-19, after
Grok's fifth re-review GRV251G); tears on Plan and Bypass say
the acknowledged mode is in effect but unconfirmed, since those modes
install no reviewer; the proof replays the recorded 1.4.7 frames through
the real session). An
unknown running mode says so. So Manual is never left running with the judge
and the menu
always agrees with the host; a finished schedule puts its mode and reviewer
back as one unit, and when the reviewer cannot be put back the session
refuses new turns while the restore gate resolves. The mode-sync
orchestration lives in the deferred bundle `dist/approvalModes.js`
(`src/core/backends/musecode/approvalModesEntry.ts`, loaded on the first
mode change, schedule admission or restore), so activation carries only
thin shells. No production path in this tree sends through the
scheduled-admission entry points (the runtime engine's delivery targets
refuse; `ScheduleAgentSession` is never constructed); the admission and
restore paths are proven by live probes. Manual's words stand unchanged;
they hold on Muse Code 1.4.7 and later. Record:
`docs/certification/manualmode.md`.

### D212 — Secondary roles: a busy role borrows an idle agent, and gives it back (M120, 2026-10-09; numbered D109 on the rig branches until the 0.19.0 join, when that number was found shared with main's D109 model-call turn limits)

The owner, 2026-10-09: "i want to be able to assign fallback roles to agents
so they have the main role but if all of a certain type of lane needs help
... a codex agent is assigned a role as a review agent and all of the coding
slots are consumed the coding could fallback to that review agent ... if the
review agent is needed its main role needs to resume priority and there
should be timers on this so an agent is not pulled ... if they have work very
soon in the pipeline and we dont want them assigned to that sub role if it
just became needed it should be a minute or longer". Lead's calls on the
name and the timers are below. This extends D103; it does not replace it.

- **The name.** Every agent (D103 candidate) has one **main role** and may
  have **secondary roles**, in order. The panel says "Main role: Review ·
  Also helps with: Coding". Lending an agent to a secondary role is
  **borrowing**; taking it back is a **recall**.
- **When a role may borrow.** All of these hold:
  - the role has a task that has waited at least the **demand wait** (60 s
    by default, never less than 60 s) with every candidate on its own
    preference list busy, capped, rate-limited or unavailable, the whole
    time (a main candidate freeing up in the window cancels the borrow);
  - the agent lists that role as a secondary role, meets the task's
    conditions (D103: platform, tools; review ≠ author), and is under its
    own caps and the team's;
  - the agent has no running task and no main-role work **due soon**: none
    of its main role's tasks is queued (at any lookahead, 0 included), and
    no running task that will produce main-role work for it (a coding lane
    that will need a review, a review that will need a fix) is expected to
    finish within the **lookahead** (10 min by default). The expected finish
    comes from the running task's time box and the role's recorded median
    duration;
  - the agent has not come back from a borrow within the **cooldown**
    (3 min by default).
- **Who is borrowed first.** The agent whose main role is idlest: the
  longest expected time to its next main-role work, then the agent's own
  secondary-role order, then the borrowing role's preference list order.
- **One task at a time.** A borrowed agent takes one task. When it ends,
  the agent returns to its main role before it can be borrowed again.
- **The main role takes it back.** Unmet main-role tasks pair with borrowed
  agents that meet their conditions by maximum bipartite matching; agents
  already asked go first, then the earliest to finish, only as a
  deterministic tie-break among maximum matchings. When main-role work
  arrives for a borrowed agent, and no other main candidate can take it:
  - a borrowed task finishes first only while `now` and its expected finish
    are both inside the **finish grace** (5 min by default) counted from
    when unmet main-role work first appeared for that agent (the earliest
    `unmetSinceMs` it can take); a task already past its expected finish
    gets no grace;
  - otherwise the agent is recalled at the task's next safe point, waiting
    at most the **recall wait** (2 min by default). The D103 handoff
    captures the work: commits, uncommitted diff, new files, a progress
    note. The task goes back to the head of its role's queue, keeping its
    place. If no safe point comes within the recall wait, the agent is
    stopped and the work is captured the same way, so nothing is lost.
  - if a main candidate frees up first, the main-role work goes there, and
    the borrow continues.
- **Review ≠ author, through borrowing.** An agent that coded a task as a
  borrowed coder never reviews that task, and neither does its engine (D103).
- **Meters and money.** A borrowed agent's use counts against its own caps
  and the borrowing role's pool caps. Paid extras still ask once before the
  first charge (D78). Borrowing never raises a cap.
- **Shown, not hidden.** The roster and the panel show "Codex: Review,
  helping with Coding (since 14:02)". Every skip has a reason ("not
  borrowed: a review is due in about 4 min"). A recall shows why. The task
  report records each borrow and each recall in the D103 chain.
- **Settings.** Each role's advanced settings hold the demand wait,
  lookahead, finish grace, recall wait and cooldown, with the defaults above.
  The demand wait cannot go below 60 s. The preference editor sets an
  agent's secondary roles by drag and drop, in every editor.
- **Defaults.** A user with no team, or with no secondary role set, sees no
  change; golden requests stay byte-identical. The built-in team templates
  set sensible secondary roles out of the box (enhancements on by default):
  `frontend` and `backend` help each other and `engineering`; `review` helps
  `engineering`. The user can clear them.
- **Fleet first.** The lead's rig fleet follows the same rules. In
  `scratchpad/rig-lanes/roles.json`, the review engine's secondary role is
  coding, with the same timers. Every borrow and recall is logged to
  `fleet-outcomes.tsv`.

### D213 — The MCP client speaks both protocol eras; the connector stays legacy (lane RLMCPERA, 2026-10-22)

The survey's MCP claims were verified against the spec and the published
SDKs before building (every source and capture:
`docs/certification/rlmcpera.md`): `2026-07-28` is current, has no
handshake, and a legacy client fails against a modern-only server. The
client probes `server/discover` at `2026-07-28` and falls back to
`initialize` (stdio on a disposable sibling process, HTTP on its own
transport instance), carries the `_meta` envelope and mirrored headers on
every modern request, retries `-32022` once at a mutual modern version,
runs MRTR elicitation through the M91 machinery, and leaves the legacy
path byte-identical. The 10 s probe silence bound is the official Python
SDK's documented probe timeout: the spec's verdict mechanism, not a
limit of ours. The connector stays legacy-only: the spec requires
nothing of legacy servers and none of its clients speaks only the new
era. Full record: `docs/certification/rlmcpera.md`.

### D214 — The stabilized ACP surface is answered, on SDK 1.8.0 (lane ACPGAPS, 2026-10-12; numbered D108 on its branch until the 0.19.0 join, when that number was found shared with the test overhaul; numbered D212 until the int/recovery join of 2026-10-22, when that number was found shared with secondary roles)

An editor that calls a stabilized method gets the documented answer, never
"method not found"; shapes rest on the pinned SDK 1.8.0 schema or a protocol
page read 2026-10-12, and stay UNVERIFIED until a real editor confirms them
(capture plan and certification record are linked in the full record). Full
record: [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D217 — Judge fast path: `stat` is reported by the helper, not started (M125 F1a, 2026-10-12; numbered D108 on its branch, D108 taken by the test overhaul, then D212 until the int/recovery join of 2026-10-23, when that number was found shared with secondary roles)

**Decision (lead, records the M125 F1a stat follow-up; design
`docs/design/judge-fast-path.md`, evidence
`docs/certification/m125-f1a.md`).** The confinement helper answers
`stat` itself from the walked operands — `statx` on the
walk-verified descriptor (`AT_EMPTY_PATH`, never resolving the path
again), re-applying the device, file-type and link-count predicates —
and prints the default report with numeric owners and UTC times. No
program is verified or executed for `stat`, and no grant beyond the
walked operands is needed, so the result cannot depend on which
coreutils implementation a distribution ships. The boundary grants
strictly less than starting the system binary did. The stat path keeps
every operand descriptor open until the report; operand opens that fail
with `EMFILE`/`ENFILE` refuse with `limits`, and a started program
killed by a signal is never read as the helper's verdict (`du`, which
dies asking for a thread the boundary denies, reports `processCreation`).
The lane-sandbox per-program table is labelled as a sandbox measurement
and decides nothing about a real desktop; the real-machine capture is
produced with `node scripts/inspect-capture.mjs` and lands by the lead's
commit. No user-facing strings: F1a refusals stay typed internal
protocol words.

### D218 — The team runner's playbook board reads live team facts (lead, 2026-10-22; lane RLM116 Q1; numbered D212 on its branch until the int/recovery re-land of 2026-10-23, when that number was found shared with secondary roles)

`readBoard` comes from the team's real facts: `workers` are its entry worker
states (available when idle and admitted) under the entry ids the offloading
caller uses; `mergedPrerequisites` are task branches merged into the
integration target, no other; `hasCi` is the CI the report engine really
observed (M113's check runs), unknown never true. The team runner starts each
file-bearing task's round at its real effect site, after every admission and
before launch, and releases it when the task ends, on the window's playbook
worker (never the extension host; on Windows inside its contained job).
`pick`/`merge` wait for the merge planner binding. Record:
`docs/certification/cc-rlm116.md`.

### D219 — Check admission reads host capacity; headless `playbook run` (lead, 2026-10-22; lane RLM116 Q2; numbered D213 on its branch until the int/recovery re-land of 2026-10-23, when that number was found shared with the MCP protocol eras)

Real capacity comes from the hosts that offload work (the ACP agent and the
team runner), never the panel, whose fail-closed port stays: a sync holder
serves the latest M107 reading, refreshed asynchronously, and admission pauses
a local check only at the governor's paused level; unknown never pauses work.
`muse-spark-code-acp playbook run <name> [--heavy] [--full-gate]` runs one
workspace check through the same admission, journal and record, with no
limits of ours (D121), and exits with the check's own code; `/playbook`
stays read-only. Record: `docs/certification/cc-rlm116.md`.

### D220 — One report ordering through `collectPlaybookReport` (lead, 2026-10-22; lane RLM116 Q3; numbered D214 on its branch until the int/recovery re-land of 2026-10-23, when that number was found shared with the stabilized ACP surface)

Playbook, milestone and fleet rows reach the M113 engine ordered by
`collectPlaybookReport` over the journal the report reads, asked for only
when one of those kinds orders; the playbook CLI text uses the same
comparator, so `orderedPlaybookRecords` and `orderReport` are one. Ordering is
presentation: `orderReport` returns its why-note and stores nothing; severity
survives the engine's key sort as a bucket prefix; milestone residuals merge
the journal's residual register through the one section builder. Record:
`docs/certification/cc-rlm116.md`.

### D221 — ACP child resumes admitted through `SubagentAdmission` (lead, 2026-10-22; lane RLM116's ACP admission follow-up; numbered D215 on its branch until the int/recovery re-land of 2026-10-23, when that number was found shared with physical device safety)

The ACP agent's only child-work effects, `/agents continue|retry`, go through
the same `SubagentAdmission` port as the Model API host, as `delegate` rounds
asked last around the control call: a refusal answers the person and reaches
no backend; without the port the control runs as before. The admission is the
host capacity of D219, refreshed on every resume; no journal is read or
written. Record: `docs/certification/cc-rlm116.md`.

### D226 — One MHP version in every native host (lead, lane RLM104, 2026-10-22; numbered D212 on its branch until the cc/rlm104 re-land of 2026-10-24)

Every native host negotiates `MHP.version` (`mhp/1.5.0`, wire `1.5`, range
to exclusive `mhp/1.6.0`) or refuses with `MHP_INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION`; no
older route, tag, schema or test survives. Both legacy-named snapshots and
locks advertise 1.5.0; a new revision regenerates every schema, lock and
host together. Record: `docs/certification/cc-rlm104.md`.

### D227 — Teams stay off until the person sets up a second model (RLF-TEAMGATE, 2026-10-23; numbered D217 on its branch until the int/recovery join of 2026-10-30, when that number was found shared with the judge fast path's `stat`)

Owner decision, verbatim: "the teams cant work with only one agent so by
that logic it should be off until a user sets up additional models".
Teams are available only while the person has at least two usable models
configured — a lead plus at least one worker the team engine can really
dispatch to, counted across backends and providers, never a raw settings
count — and the person has not switched them off. With fewer, every team
entry point refuses in words and the UI says how to enable teams (set up
another model). Nothing else is a second switch: the editor latch and the
headless certification flag are gone, and an absent `museSpark.team`
counts as on; only an explicit `false` still turns teams off. The rule is
one shared module (`src/shared/teamAvailability.ts`) used by the editor
host, the ACP agent, headless exec and the webview. Resolves M96b review
finding 4 (the single availability gate). It supersedes M96b/D208's
silent single-model parity for explicit team entry points: an explicit
`--team` without a second runnable model refuses instead of running on
silently; unasked conversations still stay single-model by the same
count. Proof: [docs/certification/rlf-teamgate.md](docs/certification/rlf-teamgate.md).

### D228 — A transiently failed request retries itself, the industry-standard way (lane RLF-AUTORETRY, owner decision 2026-10-23; numbered D217 on its branch until the int/recovery join of 2026-10-30, when that number was found shared with the judge fast path's `stat`)

The owner: "auto resend we should follow the industry standard", and "no
limits mean the limits we set it does not mean dont put any limits
obviously there needs to be limits for things like fail retries". One
retry loop per request path: the Model API backend retries the failed
model request inside the turn, keeping the conversation and every tool
result; the Muse Code backend, where the CLI owns the loop, resends a
continue in the same session from the send site (the panel controller,
the ACP agent), never re-running tools that already ran. Only transient
failures retry — connection errors and timeouts, 408, 409, 429, 5xx and
overload signals — never a refusal, an auth error or a bad request.
Backoff is exponential with jitter and honours `retry-after` /
`retry-after-ms` whole. Each provider's documented maximum and backoff
ceiling govern where documented; where a provider documents none, the
SDK default governs (2 retries, 0.5 s doubling to 8 s: `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES`,
`INITIAL_RETRY_DELAY`, `MAX_RETRY_DELAY` in openai-python and
anthropic-sdk-python `_constants.py`, read 2026-10-23; "twice by default,
honoring the retry-after header when present",
platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors; "use exponential backoff with
jitter and limit the number of retries",
developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/error-codes). The maximum is
person-settable (setting, panel, CLI flag); 0 disables. During a wait
the person sees "Retrying in Ns (attempt K of N)" with Stop, in the
panel and through ACP; Stop, a non-transient error, or the last attempt
ends it and shows the error with the Retry action (RLF-ACPTURNS). Full
record: `docs/certification/rlf-autoretry.md`. Lane scope, 2026-10-30: this
lane ships the panel-controller resend and the per-backend settings
(`museSpark.modelApiMaxRetries`, `museSpark.museCodeMaxRetries`). The
ACP agent keeps RLF-ACPTURNS's client-side retry (`data.retryable`); a
panel control and a headless flag for the maximum stay unbuilt (no
setting in the product is set from the panel today, and `exec` does
not retry). Open items with recommendations: the record above.

## 3. Open questions (need the owner)

<a id="q-cc-licence"></a>

- **Q-CC-LICENCE — two bundled packages without a licence text
  (2026-10-24).** `npm run package:acp` refuses `@npmcli/agent@5.0.2` (ISC)
  and `proxy-agent-negotiate@1.1.0` (MIT) in `dist/packsVerify.js`: neither
  package, its source revision nor its default branch carries a copyright or
  permission notice (npm/agent#123, #176; TooTallNate/proxy-agents#479 are
  open), and the notices gate takes only upstream's own text. Both arrive
  only through `@sigstore/sign`, which the verifier never runs. **Lead's
  option:** compose the verifier from `@sigstore/tuf`, `@sigstore/verify`
  and `@sigstore/bundle` as `sigstore.verify` does; measured 1,121,069 →
  207,082 bytes and 53 → 15 packages, both refused packages gone.
  **Owner's option (legal terms):** accept the standard SPDX ISC and MIT
  texts, with no invented holder or year, as their notices. Record:
  `docs/certification/cc-licence.md`.
  **Resolved by the lead (2026-10-24, cc-sigstore): the lead's option.**
  `verify.ts` composes the three packages directly (exact pins, §2 D3's
  row), `sigstore` left the dependencies, and `dist/packsVerify.js` carries
  15 package directories in 212,784 bytes with neither refused package;
  the ACP package passes its notices step. Nothing is asked of the owner.
  Record: `docs/certification/cc-sigstore.md`.

<a id="q-0191-linux-vault"></a>

- **Q-0191-LINUX-VAULT — the vault in VS Code on Linux (2026-10-20).**
  **Resolved by the owner: ship with the limitation documented, fix in the
  next release** (0.19.1; the release itself is 0.19.0). The .vsix carries no `@napi-rs/keyring` binding (about
  3.4 MB unpacked against ~200 KB of package budget headroom), so the
  extension's Linux build has no Secret Service slot, and the TPM2 slot
  probes `/dev/tpmrm0` directly, which a user outside the `tss` group cannot
  open; on a stock Linux desktop the vault therefore cannot be set up in VS
  Code (the terminal agent installs the binding and works). 0.19.0 makes the
  `storeUnavailable` sentence say this, and the CHANGELOG and README record
  it. Options for the next release: seal through `systemd-creds`' user scope (systemd
  256+, no device access), the Secret Service over D-Bus without a native
  binding, or a package budget the owner raises to ship the binding.

### D203 — `/playback`: the agent plays back its understanding, from memory only (owner, 2026-10-17)

The owner, verbatim: "i want to add a slash command /playback this should
have the agent report its current understanding of the goal, or
instructions, from its working memory no scans or files checks. the goal of
this is to give the user an accurate view of what the agent thiks vs what
the goal or instruction was so they have a way to confirm whether or not
the agent uderstood the task or whatever properly."

- **What it is.** `/playback` in the current conversation asks the agent to
  state, only from what it already holds in its working memory (the
  conversation context): the goal and the instructions and constraints it
  follows; what it has done and is doing now; what it will do next; what it
  is unsure of or assumed; and anything else that shapes how it will act
  ("etc" is everything else not mentioned). The reply opens with the fixed
  marker `My playback — my own understanding, from memory only:`, so the
  person knows it is the agent's own understanding to compare and correct.
  It takes no arguments: `/playback` with anything after it answers usage.
- **No scans, no file reads, no tools — enforced in code, not by wording.**
  The turn's prompt says what to report and that no tools are available,
  and the harness refuses every tool call in code for that turn: on the
  Model API backend (Meta and every M95 provider through it) the turn is
  offered no tools at all and `decideAndRun` refuses any call, answered to
  the model as refused, in every mode, Bypass included (the M70 Reviewer
  gate's stricter sibling). On Muse Code there is no backend-enforced
  zero-tool turn (MSP is "select, never create": no approval mode denies
  reads, and the file tools edit without asking even in Plan — SECURITY.md
  "Muse Code's file writes"), so `/playback` is refused there instead of
  sent as an ordinary turn a reactive stop might reach too late (Codex P2
  thread on PR #221, 2026-10-17). External agents get the prompt text
  only, where they accept a prompt.
- **One turn of the conversation, on the Model API backend, on every surface.** The panel
  (palette row, typed text, host message, controller turn with the send
  barrier, checkpoint and busy refusals shared with reviews), the terminal
  and ACP editors (the ACP agent's command list and prompt interception,
  which `exec` rides in-process), and other editors through the shared
  core. A message sent while a playback starts waits for it; one playback
  at a time. It is part of the user's own turn, so nothing asks for
  payment. The playback turn's text loads with the
  review bundle, as a review's does. Listed in the slash-command list, the
  Help reference and the README, with real translations in all 14
  languages.
- **How it differs from the comparables.** Claude Code's bundled skills
  and custom commands are prompt-based (`/doctor`, `/code-review`):
  detailed instructions, tools still available
  (`https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands.md`, fetched
  2026-10-17). `/playback` is the opposite trade: the prompt asks only
  for a memory report, and the harness makes tool use impossible (Model
  API; refused on Muse Code, which has no zero-tool turn), so the answer
  can only come from memory.
- Record: `docs/certification/playback.md`.

### D140 — Linux dictation helper downloads on consent; the VSIX carries no helper binaries (2026-10-10, lead decision closing Q67; numbered D106 on its branch until 2026-10-17, when that number was found shared with the MCP connector draft)

**Lead decision (2026-10-10, CM9LNX2 brief).** The native recogniser helper
is NOT packaged in the VSIX. The VSIX size and its 3,700 KiB cap stay
unchanged. Instead the helper (x64 and arm64, twelve files each:
`muse-dictate`, three libraries and the eight CPU backend variants the
`GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS` build emits, so the runtime selects the machine's
optimized backend) is built by the release workflow, attested, and
published as same-tag release assets; the build embeds each asset's
SHA-256 in the extension, generated at build time from the built helpers.

**Mechanism (this lane).** `src/shared/linuxHelperPins.ts` carries the
twenty-four pins (stable asset names under `releases/latest/download`,
exact bytes and SHA-256); it is read only by `dist/voiceLinux.js` on the
first Linux
recording, never at activation. The release workflow regenerates it with
`node scripts/build-linux-helper-pins.mjs` from both built architectures
before packaging; committed values are UNSET (bytes 0, empty digest), and an
unset build refuses every helper download before any consent card, instead
of trusting anything. `node scripts/check-linux-helper-pins.mjs` guards the
shape always, `--require-values` in the packages job, and
`--bundle dist/voice.js --assets <uploaded>` in the build and release jobs,
so a VSIX whose pinned digests do not match the uploaded assets fails. The
staging guard (`scripts/package-vsix.mjs`), `.vscodeignore` and the hosted
VSIX content check now refuse any helper binary in the package instead of
requiring it; only the licence notices stay packed.

**Acquisition.** The existing Whisper-model consent card covers both
downloads with their sizes, asked once per press (the first answer covers
helper and model). Every helper file travels the model's hardened path
(`PinnedFileDownload`: HTTPS-only redirects, identity encoding, validated
ranges/lengths, bounded streaming writes, fsync, exact size and full SHA-256
before publication, atomic lock with live/dead owner rules, symlinked
storage refusal, resumable partials). Installed files are re-hashed before
every start; the binary keeps owner-only execute permissions
(`helperMode: 0o755`), libraries owner-only data (`fileMode: 0o600`). A
digest mismatch, a partial file or a swapped file refuses loudly through the
existing integrity errors and offers retry/remove; OFF removes helper and
model with their partials. Manual install (offline users): download the
twenty-four assets plus the model file into the folder the card names;
digests are checked the same way.

**Known approximations (lead to confirm).** The card shows the measured
first-download size (~7.6 MB five-file x64 inventory) rather than the
brief's ~3 MB; the eight CPU backend variants per architecture are not in
that number yet: re-measure it from the staged release helpers before
publishing.
which was the ZIP-compressed inventory: the download is the uncompressed
files. A swapped helper binary between verification and spawn (TOCTOU) is
not closed; the window is one spawn and is recorded here. The
`latest/download` asset URL resolves to the newest release: an older
extension against newer assets refuses by digest (fail closed).

**Q-D107 answered by the owner (2026-10-10): B, with B1 and B2.** The
question (2026-10-09) was whether the judge may let clearly safe actions
skip the slow reviewer, under his standing rule (2026-09-27) that the
judge never answers the user, never writes code and is never the **sole**
gate for an action. He was told that the recommendation was A (advisory
only) plus a deterministic read-only allow list, and that B2 runs
repository code an agent may have edited; after that explanation he chose
the full fast path. A held Auto action may skip the slow reviewer only
when it passes the deterministic floor nothing overrides (forbid and ask
rules, evaluators, redirection, `sudo`, installs, destructive git,
outside or protected paths, secrets, network, paid, spawn), belongs to a
built-in class (B1 read-only inspect commands; B2 the workspace's own
unchanged check scripts), and the judge does not veto within 300 ms (no
answer is a veto; widened the same day to up to 5 s, Q-D107-VETO below);
an audit row per skip, undo through the turn's
checkpoint, kill switches, and on by default per class only after zero
harm in 400 labelled actions per class. The judge is one of two gates,
never the only one. M125's lanes F1 (B1) and F2 (B2) are planned work. Its design (D107;
`docs/design/judge-fast-path.md` §9) enforces B1's read set and B2's
containment in the operating system: B1 on Linux and macOS, B2 on Linux
only (after the fourth review, macOS cannot guarantee that no process
outlives a B2 run), both off on Windows, on Muse Code and as root.

**Q-D107-VETO answered by the owner (2026-10-10): the judge's veto window
is up to 5 s for both B1 and B2.** The question was whether the 300 ms veto
deadline could be widened, since no measured engine answers in 300 ms. He
was told that, and that 5 s is still about ten times faster than the
reviewer's 45–60 s timeouts, and chose up to 5 s for both classes over
"B2 5 s, B1 300 ms" and "300 ms for both". The window is the same for both
classes: up to 5 s from the hold, whenever B2's contained run ends; a B2
run that finishes before the judge answers waits for the answer within
those 5 s, and no answer by 5 s is a veto. (An earlier record of this
answer said B2's window ended at the earlier of the run's end and 5 s; that
was a relay error, corrected by the lead the same day.) Every other guard
is unchanged. By the lead's decision the reviewer starts when the action
is held, as today, and the cancel is sent to it as soon as the skip is
decided (when the fast path's result is delivered), so a veto or a missing
answer adds no wait; a skip saves wall time, not the tokens the
reviewer's already-started request has used (D107;
`docs/design/judge-fast-path.md` §9.3, and §9.7 for the engines that
qualify).

### D116 — A chat surface takes the keyboard only while it holds it (panel-focus, 2026-10-12; numbered D108 until 2026-10-15, when that number was found shared with the test overhaul)

**D116 — A chat surface takes the keyboard only while it holds it.** Focus
moves only as the direct effect of something the person just did on that
surface, and only while that surface still holds the keyboard when the focus
would land. A webview never focuses its composer merely because it finished
loading; async arrivals (an approval or question card, a report's arriving
headings) take the keyboard only under the same ownership. A focus request
that cannot land at once is dropped, not held: the host mints a tokened ask at
its single post gate and drops it while its panel is not the active one, and
the webview records and lands an ask only within the 1000 ms delivery window
(`docs/certification/panel-focus.md`). Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

### D205 — The panel lists exactly what the transport admits (M95, 2026-10-17)

Rule 13 keeps uncaptured presets out of the Models & Agents panel, and the
transport refuses them with no dispatch even when keyless (C-M95-4 R2). The
`custom` preset is the exception on both sides: it is the user's own server,
which the transport admits without a capture, so the panel lists it — the
milestone Goal's "a compatible server of their own". Main's union also
listed uncaptured local presets the transport refuses; the candidate's
exclusion also dropped `custom`, closing the Goal's custom-server path.
`listedPresets()` plus `custom` is the whole catalogue; the local scan
probes only listed presets. Per-attempt pool enrichment for headless exec
has no consumer (one run pins one account; `--account-pool` refuses loudly
under D88.5), so the unwired helper is removed rather than connected.

### D89.5 — Credential variables stay out of model-run processes (ENVFENCE, 2026-10-05)

The VS Code Model API shell inherited credential variables from the extension
host and terminal overrides. The shared, case-insensitive credential-name
matcher now fences shell commands, verification/`then_run`, background and
scheduled runs, child/team workers, hooks/plugins, Git and native helpers.
MCP stdio servers keep their narrow host projection and their explicitly
configured `env`; browser checks keep their private projection. Image tools
use in-process HTTP and file IO, with no child process. Muse Code's own
`serve`, account, skills and login processes keep D1's credential path.

`museSpark.shell.passEnvironmentVariables` is an empty-by-default,
machine-scoped array of variable names, never values. Only an interactive
top-level shell command (including the user's `!` command) may pass a named
credential. Unattended verification/`then_run`, schedules, child/team workers,
hooks/plugins and helpers never honor it. Moving an already admitted
interactive shell to the background preserves its starting environment.
The setting warns that a command can expose the value to the conversation
and model provider. ACP/headless keep their existing credential-free tool
environments in every editor; no pass-through flag is added there.

The base lacks `src/shared/featureCatalog.ts`: add the setting to HELPREF's
catalogue when that lane merges. No paid/live calls are authorized.

**FIXENVFENCE review repair (2026-10-05).** RVENVFENCE found two P1s:
common credential names escaped the matcher, and a scheduled shell delayed
in directory preparation could read a later active-turn state as interactive.
Cover the standard credential suffix families and known exact/prefix names,
with an explicit harmless-name allow-list. Capture interactive admission when
the command is created, before hooks or directory waits; the native spawn
still rechecks the captured owner's admission. Regressions must include a
real shell, ACP startup removal, safe-name preservation, and a backgrounded
scheduled command released after its turn ends. Deliberately break each fix,
observe the named tests fail, restore byte-exact and record the evidence in
`docs/certification/envfence.md`. No new dependency or broader exception.

  let it end, steer it) captures the real one.

  owned full-descendant shutdown proof can make native/command/hook snapshots

  that proof. Explicit confirmed removal of only a stale unsafe presence file
  preserves saved checkpoints. No paid/live capture is authorized by this
  implementation; investigate a bounded future proof separately.

  SessionEnd hooks run on purpose while the Host closes, hook settings are
  user-global and not trust gated, and Stop is honoured through the signal; the

  (Windows) be served by moving the repository? That would change the hashed
  namespace. Default: refuse with the `checkpointPathTooLong` message.
- **M72 dirty buffers in other windows:** a restore refuses a file with unsaved
  changes in the window that restores, but an idle peer window on the same folder
  publishes only that it is open, so its unsaved buffer of a file the restore
  overwrites or deletes is not known. VS Code keeps that buffer and reports the
  file changed on disk at its next save (it asks before overwriting), so nothing
  is silently lost. Should every window publish its unsaved paths in its
  presence file, so a restore refuses them too? Default: unchanged, recorded as
  a limit (Codex, `a424e526`).

Minimal completion design under D81.3:

1. Reuse the existing Model API tool-loop boundary after a completed todo
   transition and the existing context/usage and compaction primitives.
   Decide once at a settled boundary, using the supported model's existing
   cache prices and window limit; do not create a scheduler or a second
   compaction engine. No autonomous work after the user's turn ends.
2. Snapshot the exact open todos, goal and untrusted-content provenance.
   Preserve these separately from the generated summary, then restore the
   exact list before another request. A hidden model restatement must have
   an explicit cost/consent contract, run through the same M82 account/key,
   cap, Stop and final-send checks, and may not replace the authoritative
   list with a lossy model guess.
3. A memory flush uses the existing MemoryStore and permission engine:
   Manual asks, Plan and Restricted Mode refuse, and notes derived from
   tool/fetched/imported content retain an untrusted label. If generating
   those notes adds a model call beyond the user's turn, use the existing
   paid gate and paid-use popup with its own explicit feature/price and
   usage row; do not reuse another paid feature's grant or hide the cost.
4. Build one M75 arm on the current verified harness. Freeze long-context
   accept/held-out tasks before running it, exercise todo preservation,
   provenance, memory refusals and Stop, and require actual compaction
   evidence as well as both 0.75 capability floors. Only a passing current
   pair permits production activation; D81.3 supersedes the original
   off-by-default setting with a default-on setting behind the evaluation latch.
   Record paid attempts,
   known/unknown usage, source hashes and the incomplete inventory honestly.

### Q-M114S — Historical page-mount timeout provenance (2026-10-06)

The prior 4,752-capture log has no scene key, trace or resource measurements.
Its recorded loop order bounds the failure to Dracula/690 px/English in the
last 72-capture batch; the exact scene within that batch is not known.
Continuation 3's complete diagnostic passes 4,824 captures, and 500 repeated
late Tasks mounts do not reproduce a two-second stall. The capture driver now
names scene/theme/width/English and page errors on a failed mount. The exact
historical scenario and cause remain unconfirmed; a trace/resource log from
that run is requested. Do not infer a scene from the last progress batch or
describe the timeout as fixed merely because a later run passes. New CI shards
bound each source/candidate replay to 804 captures; repeated full receipts
certify their own rendering results, not an unknown historical root cause.

**H-M114S-report-readiness → harness scenario owner.** A separate source
reconstruction compares 216 captures before `report-narrow/light/320/en`
throws `never rendered: .report-check input`. Delaying only the report lazy
chunk reproduces that exact error while one deferred-loading fallback is
present and no checkbox has mounted: the harness's 3,000 ms virtual deadline
expires in 261 ms of real time. The controlled probe demonstrates a readiness
race; it does not identify the older root timeout. Two attempted owned
barriers (400 ms start followed by checkbox readiness, then network-idle
readiness) both fail the default 10-second setup deadline. Stop that path
under the shared rule; remove the experimental test and restore the capture
driver SHA-256-exact. The proposed exact harness fix is a report-scenario
completion marker after DOM readiness and the existing spacing assertion,
awaited under the real page deadline before advancing its virtual deadline.
Preserve missing-control failure and compatibility with the recorded source
harness. This foreign contract change remains unimplemented and unverified.
See `docs/certification/m114-s-after/c3-report-readiness.json`.

The second complete replay also records `history-archived/dracula/690/en`
failing `whenFound('.history-toggle input')` inside `clock.runFor`, with no
page errors. Include this lazy history scenario in the same harness
readiness-contract handoff; its uncaptured resource timing is unconfirmed.
The complete receipt retains that failed batch attempt and its retry.

**H-M114S-code-highlight-readiness → webview/harness owner.** Batch 6's
first attempt fails at `markdown/dracula/690/en`: 475 changed pixels, all
within the code text at x=38–432, y=260–290. The candidate is plain text

`HighlightedCode` Suspense fallback has no pending marker, so the owned

contract with clock coordination, and retain intentionally plain open or
unknown-language blocks. Support or re-review the recorded source harness.
No production webview file is edited here. The next attempt passes under
the unchanged policy; the failed attempt remains evidence, not a red drill.

## 4. Architecture

```
VS Code extension host (Node)
  src/extension.ts             activate(): the view, the panel, the commands, the
                               output and file openers, the usage cache
  src/host/                    VS Code-facing adapters
    views/                     the WebviewView (sidebar) and WebviewPanel (editor
                               tab); the zod-validated postMessage bridge
    conversation/              ConversationController: one panel's session, turns,
                               approvals, questions, edits, rewind, usage, references
    backend/                   MuseCodeBackendManager (spawns `muse serve`), the
                               Model API tool harness (toolIo, searchWorker), the
                               file session store
    auth/                      SecretStorage for the key; `muse login` in a terminal
    editor/, mention/          open-file context, @mention search, diff documents
    commands/, settings.ts     the commands; museSpark.* readers with defaults
    voice/, usage/, ide/       the dictation helper host; trace-log insights; the
                               loopback MCP server that serves getDiagnostics
  src/core/                    backend-agnostic, no `vscode` import
    agent/agentBackend.ts      AgentHost / AgentSession: startSession, sendTurn,
                               cancel, setModel, setReasoningEffort, setApprovalMode,
                               listModels, listSessions, resumeSession, forkSession,
                               compact, decideApproval, answerQuestions,
                               cancelQuestions, controlSubagent, messageSubagent
    backends/musecode/         the MSP adapter over @muse-code/sdk (MuseCodeHost,
                               launch, notification mapping, session records)
    backends/modelapi/         fetch + SSE client, the tools, the permission engine
                               that reproduces the approval-mode semantics
    context/, usage/, voice/   rules, skills and memory loading; trace-log parsing;
                               the dictation driver
  src/shared/                  constants, the zod protocol, agentEvents (turnStarted,
                               textDelta, reasoningDelta, toolStarted, …), palette,
                               effort, permission modes, sessions, usage
                                 │ postMessage (zod-validated both ways)
Webview (browser, React 19)
  src/webview/main.tsx         mount, theme tokens from VS Code CSS variables
    App.tsx                    the panel: transcript scroll, menus, dialogs, wiring
    components/Composer        input, "+" attach, "/" palette, @mention, chips,
                               model/effort pill, permission-mode button, send/stop
    components/Transcript,     streaming markdown, code blocks (copy/insert/apply),
      ToolRow, ReasoningRow    tool rows with diffs and outputs, thinking rows
    components/ApprovalCard,   approval and question cards, the reply and quote
      QuestionCard, QuoteMenu  menus
    components/HistoryDialog,  history; account & usage; the Agent map with its
      UsageDialog, AgentMap    owner controls
    state/uiState.ts           reducer over the AgentEvent stream
```

Key parity mapping (Claude Code UI → MSP method) is recorded in §5.

## 5. Research and version-verification notes

Full notes with URLs were gathered on 2026-09-21 and are summarised here so the
rationale survives without the research transcript.

### 5.1 Muse Spark and the Meta Model API (official sources: dev.meta.ai, ai.meta.com, research.meta.ai)

- Model IDs: `muse-spark-1.3` (current), `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`,
  `muse-spark-1.2`, `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.1`.
  No Pro/Mini variants; `reasoning_effort` is the quality axis.
- Context 1,048,576 tokens; max output 131,072; images ≤ 50 per request;
  PDFs first 50 pages.
- Base URL `https://api.meta.ai/v1`; `POST /responses` (recommended, keeps
  reasoning across tool turns via `previous_response_id` or
  `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`), `POST /chat/completions`,
  `POST /messages` (Anthropic-compatible), `GET /models`, `GET /status`,
  `POST /responses/input_tokens`.
- Auth `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; keys look like `LLM_…` (older keys
  `LLM|<id>|<secret>`).
- `reasoning_effort` ∈ `minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max`; `none` is a 400;
  `max` only on Standard-tier 1.3. Reasoning summaries via `reasoning.summary`.
- Tools: function tools, parallel by default, **`tool_choice` only `"auto"`**.
- Prompt caching automatic; `prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_retention: "24h"`.
- Pricing: Standard $1.25 / $0.15 cached / $4.25 per 1M tokens, 3,000 RPM,
  4M TPM. Contributor $0.10 / $0.002 / $0.20, 100 RPM, 3M TPM, **Meta trains on
  content**.
- ToS (2026-09-18): keys must not be shared or embedded; Integrated Products
  need a privacy policy and AI disclosure; users 18+; no reverse engineering
  of harnesses; do not imply Meta endorsement.
- There is **no official OAuth / device-code flow** for third parties.
  Muse Code subscription credentials are "for use with Muse Code only".

### 5.2 Muse Code CLI and `@muse-code/sdk` 1.3.0

- CLI: closed source; install `curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh`
  or `irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex`; auth precedence
  `META_API_KEY` env → stored key → stored browser session; `muse login`,
  `muse auth set`, `muse logout`. `muse serve` hosts MSP over stdio.
- SDK imports used: `Connection`, `MspError`, `spawnMspConnection` and the
  `FingerprintWarning` type. The raw connection supplies commands,
  notifications and server-request handlers; the spawned handshake supplies
  `initialize({clientInfo, capabilities})`. The extension does not import
  `SessionFold` or `checkServedFingerprint`; tests reference only
  `EXPECTED_SCHEMA_FINGERPRINT`.
- Wire vocabulary (from the package's `msp.d.ts`, authoritative over the
  summarised docs): methods `session/start|resume|fork|list|read|compact|
setModel|rename|setReasoningEffort|setApprovalMode|userShell`,
  `turn/start|steer|interrupt|cancel`, `model/list`, `skill/list`,
  `approval/decide`, `userInput/answer`, `usage/read`, `item/readOutput`,
  `task/*`, `subagent/*`; notifications `turn/*`, `item/started|delta|updated|
completed`, `approval/*`, `userInput/*`, `session/*Changed`,
  `session/tokenUsage`, `session/contextUsage`, `usage/changed`; server
  requests `approval/request`, `userInput/request`.
- Enumerations: `ItemKind` = userMessage | agentMessage | reasoning | toolCall
  | userShell | subagent | workflow | reminderChild | compaction;
  `ApprovalMode` = allowAll | promptUnmatched | onRequest | denyUnmatched;
  `ReasoningEffort` = none | minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh | max |
  ultra; `TurnInputPart.type` = text | image (base64Data, mediaType, width,
  height) | skill (selector, arguments); `ApprovalChoice.scope` = once |
  session | localPersistent.

### 5.3 Claude Code VS Code extension parity inventory (code.claude.com/docs)

P0 for v1: sidebar + editor-tab panel; session history with search and
auto-titles; selection and open-file context chips; `@` fuzzy file mention;
attachments (files, images via paste/drag) with `name W×H` chips; `/` palette
with grouped sections (Context / Model / Customize / Account & usage / Skills /
Slash commands / Support) and "Filter actions…" search; model pill
"Model (ctx) Effort" with picker and effort slider; permission modes (Manual,
Edit automatically, Plan, Auto, Bypass); streaming markdown with highlighted
code and Copy / Insert / Apply; native diff viewer with Accept / Reject;
permission cards (Allow once / Always allow + scope / Deny); question cards;
keybindings Ctrl+Esc (focus), Ctrl+Shift+Esc (new tab), Alt+K (insert
`@file#lines`), Ctrl+Alt+F (focus view), Alt+T (toggle extended thinking, bound here as
Ctrl+Alt+T on Windows and Ctrl+Alt+O on Linux because Alt+T is a Windows
menu mnemonic;
Ctrl+O is the CLI's transcript toggle, not a VS Code binding);
browser-based sign-in; `claudeCode.*`-style settings incl. initial permission
mode. P1: tool rows, thinking blocks, plan approval, context %, usage panel,
/compact. P2: rewind/fork, voice, /btw, agent map, session groups.

Second docs pass (2026-09-21, every page under code.claude.com/docs that
touches the VS Code composer, plus the owner's screenshots of Claude Code,
kept outside the repository since the 2026-09-23 cleanup): the composer bar is `+` (menu: Upload from computer / Add
context / Browse the web), `/`, a prompt-cache clock ("59m"), an "N agents"
pill, the model pill `Model Effort` (no context window in the pill), the
open-file chip (`PLAN.md ×`), the mode button (`⚡ Auto`) that opens a Modes
menu (Manual / Edit automatically / Plan / Auto with one-line descriptions,
`⇧ + tab to switch`, an Effort row; Bypass only with
`allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`), a microphone, and Send / Stop; the
placeholder reads "Queue another message…" while a turn runs. Items with no
Muse counterpart, verified and left out: **Browse the web** (needs the Claude
in Chrome extension), the **prompt-cache clock** (no MSP cache-TTL signal;
`session/tokenUsage` reports cached tokens only), the `/` menu's Output
styles / Hooks / Permissions rules / Memory / Instructions / MCP / Remote
Control entries (no MSP methods; Muse Code manages these in its own config),
and the `!` shell prefix (not offered by the Claude Code extension either).
Deferred, not dropped: the "N agents" pill (`subagent/*`, M4/M6), the
open-file chip (M5), the microphone (M9, Q4; Claude's is "Tap or hold to
record Ctrl+D", recording in the CLI and transcribing on Anthropic's servers
at no charge to the user; ours recognises on the machine).

Parity mapping to MSP: model pill → `model/list` + `session/setModel`; effort
→ `session/setReasoningEffort`; permission mode → `session/setApprovalMode`;
Stop → `turn/cancel` then `turn/interrupt`; history → `session/list|read|
resume`; rename → `session/rename`; rewind/fork → `session/fork`; /compact →
`session/compact`; todo panel → `session/todoListChanged`; context % →
`session/contextUsage`; usage → `usage/read`; permission cards →
`approval/request`; questions → `userInput/request`; tool rows → `toolCall`
items + `item/readOutput`; skills → `skill/list` + `skill` input part;
"!" shell → `session/userShell`; agent map → `subagent/*`, `task/*`.

### 5.4 Live MSP smoke test (Windows, 2026-09-22, signed-in CLI)

Script: session scratchpad `sdk-probe/echo-smoke2.mjs` over `@muse-code/sdk` 1.3.0
against Muse Code 1.3.0-R3401.1, both spawn modes (D1a). Observed:

- `initialize` → `session/start` → `turn/start` → streamed `item/delta`
  (`{ itemId, field: "text", delta }`) → `turn/completed`
  (`terminal: "completed", durationMs: 11214, timeToFirstTokenMs: 5123`).
- **The host's default session model is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`** (the
  training-consent tier). The extension must always pass `modelId` on
  `session/start` and default to `muse-spark-1.3`; contributor stays opt-in
  (D4).
- `model/list` returns `providerId: "meta"`, entries with `contextLimit:
1007997`, `outputLimit: 128000`, `cost: { input: "1.25", output: "4.25",
cached: "0.15", currency: "USD" }`, `isDefault`, `isActive`, `releaseDate`.
- Default `approvalMode.mode` is `onRequest`. Session files live under
  `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/<sessionId>/session.jsonl` (also
  on Windows).
- Item kinds seen in one turn: `userMessage` (completed immediately),
  `reminderChild` (host-internal, in progress → completed), `agentMessage`
  (started → delta → completed). `session/tokenUsage` (inputTokens 20804,
  cachedTokens 10481, outputTokens 210) and `session/contextUsage`
  (`windowTokens: 1007997, usedTokens: 21014, pressure: "normal"`) arrive after
  the message completes.
- `usage/read` returned `{}` for this pay-as-you-go account (no subscription
  window); the Account & usage panel must render token totals in that case.
- On `close()`: `session/closed { reason: "hostShutdown" }`, then
  `session/statusChanged { status: "notLoaded" }`, child exit code 0.
- The SDK's `SpawnedMspConnection` did not expose `serverInfo`/`museHome`/
  `fingerprint` on the object returned by `initialize` in this build (all
  `undefined`); read them from the raw `initialize` result instead (verify at
  M2).
- A hung run left a `muse-bin` child alive after the Node parent exited; the
  extension must track the child PID and kill the tree on dispose.

### RLFAUTORETRY — Automatic retry of a transiently failed request, the industry-standard way (D228)

**Status 2026-10-30: built.** The Model API backend retries the failed
model request inside the turn and the Muse Code backend resends a
retryable failed turn in the same session, transient failures only,
with industry backoff and full retry-after waits; every wait shows

waits also through ACP), and the per-backend maxima are
person-settable (`0` disables). Record:
`docs/certification/rlf-autoretry.md`. The forwarding-proxy proof, an
ACP-agent-internal resend, a panel control and a headless flag stay
open for the lead (items in the record).

**Status 2026-10-30 (integration into int/recovery, CC-INT5): built.** On
int the lane's retry policy sits in int's refactored retry loops
(`isStreamRetried`, `isStreamResent`): the limit is a number everywhere (the
person's, else the provider's documented one, else the SDK default), and an
ambiguous send is resent only within an explicit bound. The Muse Code resend
and the shared `resubmitRememberedTurn` ride int's conversation deps through
`composeConversationDeps`. `museCodeAutoResend` (a recorded exchange),
`providerRetryLimits` (real refused sends), `turnRetryCeiling`,
`turnRetryResubmit` and `acpTranslate` pass on the merged tree; no provider
request was made. Record: `docs/certification/cc-int5.md`.

**Status 2026-10-11: building.** Typed translated stop first; tools-disabled

**LEDGER (2026-10-12, Kubuntu and macmini; M80/M82/M95 repair). Superseded
2026-10-17 by D208:** the versioned ledger, its atomic admission and its
journal files are removed; spending is checked only against a limit the
person set. The original scope follows. Replace directory-per-claim budgeting with one versioned spend ledger and atomic admission for session, editor daily and terminal daily scopes; retain every sent attempt at its full liability, recover only from process identity evidence, and certify real-process races, crashes, migration and packed-product refusals. Design and ruling R9 compatibility limits: `docs/certification/spend-ledger.md`. Shared daily input reserves the byte/context bound even when terminal admission uses a provider estimate. One flushed transaction inode supplies atomic snapshot and audit/history aliases; process owner notes are cached per scope. Portable ledger errors stay in each caller's language state. Runtime settlement uses typed HTTP observations, never retry-message text, and only refunds initial rejections before response frames. Removing inherited stand-in suites also removes their unused production-only exports (unbound account-home factory, account admission wrapper and schedule paid-scope factories); their live interfaces remain. Provider endpoint/path utilities move to a leaf module to break the measured configured-bundle command cycle. Keyless configured runs bind an empty in-memory secret store and skip Meta readiness lookup; a real ECONNREFUSED before connection releases the hold. ### RLVAULTANCHOR — The vault's rollback anchor isolated per vault (2026-10-21)

**Status 2026-10-22: built.** Every record a vault
writes under the product's OS-store service is keyed to its canonical
broker root, with the pre-scoping names kept as adopted fallbacks, so an
existing vault keeps its records exactly where they were while a vault
anywhere else can never read or write them; every vault fixture removes
its own records on disposal. Status evidence:
`docs/certification/rlvaultanchor.md`. The real-store scope cases are
written and run in the hosts job on every platform; this lane's container
cannot start D-Bus, so the Secret Service proof runs outside it.

- **Goal.** The rollback anchor, the audit checkpoint and pending intent,
  and the OS-store slot keys live under per-root accounts; a vault in a
  test's folder never touches the person's real anchor, and `vault status`
  no longer reports a never-set-up vault as lost.
- **Compatibility.** A vault that wrote its records before scoping adopts
  them by vault id and keeps reading and writing them; nothing migrates
  and no reset is needed.

(Q-D107-B1-MAC), any model download (owner's go), the V-report
persistence behind the savings row, `check:catches` and knip (both
fail identically on the M98P2 base), and the packed-product real-life
run before release.

**Status 2026-10-23 (RVINT4): built.** The fourth integration round
(`8ae18f2266..2640d6daea`) kept both sides of each lane merge except
one dropped proof. Merge `47562e98c7` lost the only test that a
signaled program's stderr is not the helper's verdict. The runner
still refuses that case (`confinement`, or `processCreation` for
`du`) in `src/core/judge/fast/inspectExec.ts`. The proof is back in
`test/unit/inspectNative.test.ts`: it fails when the runner reads the
forged refusal (vitest exit 1, reason `network`) and passes on Linux
after the restore (vitest exit 0). Windows does not run that branch.
Evidence: `docs/certification/rvint4.md`.

- **Goal.** D107: the judge is our own Jev. A batched, calibrated decision
  engine makes the agent faster (decisions the big model spends a turn or
  a round-trip on) and more accurate (checks on its own work), works out
  of the box through the Set Up Local Judge wizard, and its wins are
  measured and shown.
- **Depends on.** `m98/p2-r4` merged (contract, 2b, 2c, 2e, 2i, 2j, usage
  rows, Judge section; lanes J and L change 2j and 2b with M98's owner);
  M73 (packing); M75 (paired runner); M78 (the Model API reviewer fence
  lanes F1 and F2 extend) and M90 (Muse Code's reviewer, unchanged); the
  process registry and M107's tickets (their live-process condition); M86 (the turn checkpoint);
  M91-G's raw-body harness; M95
  (provider capability records); D84's MHP command mapping (the wizard in
  other editors); D90.27's table schema and licence step (lane H builds
  them). Q-D107 is answered (B), so lanes F1 and F2 are built; Q-D107-VETO is
  answered (a veto window of up to 5 s for both classes).
- **Order.** Lanes 0 and R first (day one needs only them), then E, H, J
  and L, then W, K, M, C and P, then U and V; F1 after 0, R, E and K; F2 after F1's helper, never
  blocking F1; D closes last.
  M110's lane TJ starts after lane H merges and reuses its module.
- **Owner engine.** Left blank for every lane; the lead assigns one at
  launch.
