- **Acceptance.**
  1. With `off`, and with every decision abstaining, Model API golden
     requests and Muse Code main-session MSP frames are byte-identical (red
     drill: one decision forced to apply).
  2. A default user (no GPU, no Ollama, subscription only) gets the
     deterministic checks with no download, key, network call or prompt; the
     first-run card shows once; the Status line shows the judge's state with
     one click to the wizard. An existing verified local judge is used with
     no prompt.
  3. No I or S decision dispatches to the chat model (a test fails if one
     does); its fallback use is batched and background only.
  4. Each decision meets its deadline or falls back to today's behaviour; a
     late answer is never applied (drill: an engine that answers after its
     deadline); a deterministic miss reaches the engine within the same
     deadline, and a recognised case is never overruled.
  5. The resolver skips an engine that `eligible` rejects and readmits it
     through the real reprobe (local) or sample expiry (hosted), on a fake
     clock; its samples are complete calls (2j's verified path for local
     engines), every attempt counted and a miss as infinite. An engine with
     50 fast answers that then only times out is suspended by its third
     miss and readmitted only by three consecutive in-budget probes. An unloaded model (fresh `/api/ps: []`, keep-alive expiry)
     recovers only through the consented, bounded, cancellable preload on
     2j's actual path, and 2j's served-digest check is unchanged.
  6. Context selection and triage change only the tail or the first send;
     no earlier request byte changes (drill: a selection that edits
     history); `ide` triage is off on Muse Code. An engine triages before
     first send only at I or in a real S window; a lone shell output with
     no window goes out whole; fakes release each output at its real
     boundary, never with an answer seeded while the tool runs.
  7. Effort is only ever lowered, and only as a request field (Model API,
     M95); an abstention sends today's bytes. On Muse Code no judge
     decision sends an effort frame (MSP frame golden; drill: a decision
     that sends one fails).
  8. Confidential workspaces use deterministic checks and verified local
     engines only; the wizard offers no hosted engine there.
  9. Wizard scan and recommendation: lane H's fixtures give the expected
     backend, recommendation and plain-words reasons per hardware class (no
     GPU with 8 GB and 16 GB, NVIDIA with 8 GB of VRAM, an old NVIDIA
     driver, AMD on ROCm, Apple silicon, too small); the too-slow case
     offers Jev and Clef with price and daily budget; the benchmark stays
     within its budget; a table row without a source or date fails its
     schema; a platform without verified-path timings is not recommended;
     the classes a recommendation names equal `eligible` on the row's p95
     (drill: a 0.36 s engine named for I fails).
  10. Wizard install: nothing is downloaded, written or started before
      **Install** (network and file spies); the consent screen names what,
      where, size and time; a SHA-256 mismatch stops the step; an
      interrupted download resumes; **Cancel** and **Set Up Later** work at
      every step; nothing outside the extension's storage changes without
      the Advanced machine-wide choice (drill: a setup that writes a PATH
      entry or a service fails the spy); from `/api/ps: []` the preload
      runs before registration and cancels cleanly; the health check and
      ten-question smoke run through the verified path; Done's class states
      equal `eligible` on the smoke's p95 and its check states follow the
      profiles (drill: a Done showing a class On over its budget fails); **Remove** leaves a model or an
      Ollama the user already had (drill); a changed hardware fingerprint
      shows **Re-scan** and downloads nothing.
  11. Each accuracy check shows a hint or note only above a threshold from
      a lane L profile fitted for that engine identity and family, with its
      precision bar met; below it, or with no profile, log only. 2b still
      rejects unknown families and techniques and non-binary labels; a
      smoke never creates a profile.
  12. Each decision's M75 arm reports wall time, calls avoided, tokens
      saved, precision, recall and harm per backend and model; a decision is
      on by default only where its win is positive, its bar holds, turn
      wall time does not regress, and its cache misses on material already
      sent (`cacheMissTokens`' definition) do not rise against the paired
      off arm; a triage arm with fewer cached tokens and a hint arm with a
      few more uncached tail tokens, each with no extra misses, pass
      (drills: a gate on absolute cached tokens fails the first, a gate on
      uncached input per request fails the second); new tail tokens count
      in the per-turn totals.
  13. Account & usage shows the judge's time saved (per turn), tokens,

**RVM124 review fixes (2026-10-09, branch `feature/m124-fix`).** The
review's P1 and P2 findings 2–14 are fixed with a regression test each

**M124R3 redesign (2026-10-09, branch `feature/m124-r3`).** The second
review (RVM124B: 1 P1, 4 P2) was the third round on this module, so the
registry was redesigned rather than patched (design §3a). Every call is one
operation on one transition table under one synchronous authority (the
call's cancellation and deadline, disconnect, the kill switch, and the
grant's generation, scopes, workspace or user library and confidential
policy), checked by one gate immediately before each effect and again before
a result is delivered, with no await between gate and effect; every
transition writes one receipt. Closed: the P1 (an approved write after
revocation, kill or disconnect during the dispatch receipt wait), P2-2
(leases after cancellation), P2-3 (the limits lock now follows M123's
`storeLock` protocol with a generation fence; age never counts), P2-4 (one
receipt for every refusal, transport and control receipts) and P2-5 (Stop
follows the operation's scope), plus RVM124 finding 16 (setup docs). 29
regression cases fail on `2fa594639`; 26 red drills. Open: RVM124 finding 15
(storage ownership, Windows DACL). `dist/connector.js` 99,825 bytes of 100
KiB; `dist/extension.js` unchanged. Record:
[`docs/certification/m124-local.md`](docs/certification/m124-local.md).

| From → to                                                      | When                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `received` → `admitted` / `refused` / `cancelled`              | Admission (kill switch, rate token, strict input, grant, scope, confidential policy, durable admitted receipt) or not                                                                   |
| `admitted` → `dispatching`                                     | A read, retry, status or Stop: the gate passed; its lease or owner port starts in that tick                                                                                             |
| `admitted` → `awaitingApproval`                                | A write: durable intent receipt, pending lease, our page holds the exact intent                                                                                                         |
| `admitted` → `refused` / `cancelled` / `failed`                | Reused request id, stale target, no room, receipt failure / the authority stopped it / an owner read failed                                                                             |
| `awaitingApproval` → `approved`                                | Our page approved the shown digest and the approved receipt is durable                                                                                                                  |
| `awaitingApproval` → `cancelled` / `refused` / `failed`        | Denied, expired, Stop, disconnect, revocation, kill switch, client cancel / no approval surface / receipt or owner failure                                                              |
| `approved` → `dispatching`                                     | Dispatch receipt written ahead, target re-read, then the authority re-read as the last wait; final gate and CAS: the write starts                                                       |
| `approved` → `cancelled` / `failed`                            | The final gate refused / the receipt or the target re-read failed                                                                                                                       |
| `dispatching` → `settled` / `refused` / `cancelled` / `failed` | A read past its delivery gate with a durable settled receipt, or a returned write / result over 64 KiB or withheld / a read before its delivery gate / owner or settled-receipt failure |

`settled`, `refused`, `cancelled` and `failed` are terminal; a started write
or a committed read result is never cancelled (Stop answers
`stopRequested`).

**M124 round 4 (2026-10-09, same branch).** The review of the redesign
(RVM124R3: 1 P1, 4 P2) found the defect class one level down: acting on
authority captured before a wait. Closed: the final gate reads a live
authority (`AuthorityPort`: the store's is updated on a file-system notice
for the grant or kill-switch file and re-read as the last wait before every
final gate; an older reading never overwrites a newer one), after the
target re-read, so revocation, the kill switch, a replaced scope or a
removed workspace or user library during that re-read writes nothing (P1);
admitted, awaiting-approval, approved, dispatching and a read's settled
receipts are written ahead and fail closed, and `move` refuses those
transitions without them (P2-2); the whole call, delivery included, races
its operation's end and the connection's close (P2-3); the transport never
waits for the journal, whose best-effort receipts are tallied with a
`count` under a full backlog, so Stop is never queued behind receipts
(P2-4); only an edge of the table is journaled (finding 5). 20 regression
cases fail on `ddd7d8da3`; 37 red drills. RVM124 finding 15 stays open
(what remains is in the record). `dist/connector.js` 101,671 bytes of 100
KiB; `dist/extension.js` unchanged.

**M124 round 5 (2026-10-09, same branch).** The review of round 4
(RVM124R4: 0 P1, 3 P2). Closed: the final gate is the operation's
synchronous `gate`, called by the effect's own caller after its last
await, with the move into `dispatching` and the effect's start in the same
synchronous block; a failed move aborts the effect and ends the call
`failed` (P2-1); a committed read keeps its receipt, but a cancellation,
the deadline or a disconnect answers the call at once while the receipt
finishes in the background under the journal's timeout, and the read's
slot is freed when the owner read returns (P2-2); the runtime stops the
calls at disconnect, then finishes only after its pending operations have
ended (at most one call deadline) and the approval page's start-up has
settled, closing the page and opening no browser late (P2-3). 9 new
regression cases, 8 failing on `50962f773`; 50 red drills, all restored
byte-exact (two that first stayed green led to two snapshot-authority read
cases and the removal of a redundant runtime disconnect). RVM124 finding 15
stays open (unchanged list in the record). `dist/connector.js` 102,321
bytes of 100 KiB (79 bytes left; no cap raised); `dist/extension.js`
unchanged.

**M124 round 6 (2026-10-09, same branch; RVM124R5 P2-1).** Closed: an
opener rejection still refuses the call with `approval_unavailable`, but
the runtime keeps the successfully started approval page's promise and
closes its listener and idle timer on stdin end before returning. The
regression uses the real entry, registry, store and approval server;
103 connector tests pass natively on Windows, and a deliberate removal
of the ownership guard fails the new case, restored byte-exact.
`dist/connector.js` is 102,335 bytes of 100 KiB (65 bytes left; no cap
raised); `dist/extension.js` is unchanged. Storage ownership and Windows
DACL (RVM124 finding 15) remain deferred. Record:
[`docs/certification/m124-local.md`](docs/certification/m124-local.md).
Aggregate quality remains with the lead under the rig/common brief.

**M124 round 7 (2026-10-09, same branch; RVM124R6C P2-1).** Closed: the
approval page has one runtime-owned lifecycle: `none` → `starting` →
`open` → `closed`, with `closed` → `starting` on the next request. Idle
expiry, `EPANEL_CLOSED` and an opener failure after startup retire the page;
shutdown closes an open or starting page and still waits for registry drain.
Two recovery regressions use the real entry, grant/store, registry and
companion server, shortening only the first page's idle delay in the test;
both fail on `2786f64ec`. Round 6's rejected-opener shutdown case now proves
immediate listener retirement too. All 105 connector tests pass natively on
Windows at repository deadlines; three red drills fail their intended
assertions and restore byte-exact. Remove only the embedded page script's
392 indentation bytes to make room; its minified executable hash is unchanged.
Storage ownership/Windows DACL (finding 15), shared approval UI, real-client
qualification and hosted transport remain deferred; aggregate quality stays
with the lead. Receipts: `docs/certification/m124-local.md`, round 7.

- **Goal.** Other agents can inspect the user's fleet and evidence, request
  bounded orchestration, ask for deterministic advice/reports, and manage
  schedules/prompts/shares through one connector. Every effect goes through
  Muse Spark Code's own approval UI; every result and audit record is scrubbed.
- **Depends on.** M96/M96c's board, runtime dispatch and Agent map;
  D101/M119's outcome mapping and receipts (released in 0.16.0), which live
  inside the running session (Agent map, ACP `/agents`): no cross-process
  outcome store exists that a separate connector process can read, so the
  outcome and receipt tools say `unavailable` until their owner exports one;
  M116's placement/playbook; M117's estimator; M113's reporting; M115's
  schedule grants; M118's prompt/share engine; M104's MHP and companion
  approvals; D61/D89's secret ownership and D89.5's child fence. **Remote
  (the hosted phase):** (a) M110's home node (D90; planned, nothing
  implemented); (b) the paired-node link of D90.8 on D80.3's session protocol
  (M100; planned); and (c) an orchestrator-link command contract: how a home
  node forwards a connector intent, its approval (D90.3, through D90.10's
  approval forwarding), identities, epochs, ownership and revocation to the
  orchestrator. No PLAN decision or source defines (c) yet; it is owned by
  M110 lane 0's threat model and contracts, and M124 does not invent it.
  M103/D83 only for optional fixed machine Stop. No unmerged dependency is
  silently emulated.
- **Scope.** D106 and design §§2–8. Contracts/fakes can start first;
  adapters join only as their owners certify their seams. Local MVP is
  read-only, then approved controls; remote follows with OAuth, per-device
  grants, audit and kill switch. Meta AI stays waiting for early access.
- **Lanes and file ownership.** One integration branch,
  `feature/m124-connector`, under M87's region rules. Lane 0 freezes
  contracts and owns shared schemas/strings. Other lanes edit only their listed
  files and coordinated regions; the lead integrates and owns final quality.
  The local stdio phase (lanes 0, S, T, A and J, with H's client setup) is
  under way on that branch; R, O and the hosted qualification rows wait for
  D106.3's three dependencies.

- **Acceptance** (details and platform rows in design §8):
  1. Same strict schemas and tool policies on stdio/HTTP; malformed/oversized
     input, unknown fields, unauthorized handles and unavailable dependencies
     cause explicit errors with no effect. Client hints never decide a class.
  2. Fleet/outcome/receipt projections distinguish running, completed,
     verified, failed and unknown; an exit code or turn completion alone is not
     successful work. Reads are deterministic, paged, scoped and scrubbed.
  3. Every write/run is inert before our UI approves; Bypass, Allow always,
     elicitation and model-supplied `confirm` cannot approve. Expiry, disconnect,
     target/payload/epoch changes and revocation deny; duplicate request keys
     cannot dispatch twice. Missing UI returns `approval_unavailable`.
  4. Stop passes while approval queues, ordinary limits/budgets and the kill
     switch block other effects, and reports unreachable/uncertain truthfully.
     Cross-owner Stop is refused. D83's nested physical refusals hold.
  5. Paid authority defaults off; rates, per-use consent and both caps precede
     dispatch; reservations retain uncertainty. A schedule gets its own M115
     grant in our UI, never manufactures consent for subsequent connector calls.
  6. OAuth discovery/login/refresh works in separately captured ChatGPT and
     claude.ai flows. Wrong issuer/audience/scope/device, PKCE replay, revoked
     grant and malicious registration/metadata redirects fail before dispatch.
  7. Audit covers all calls and outcomes; planted secrets, registered literals,
     private paths/accounts and raw stderr are absent from every output channel.
     Audit failure stops new effects; Stop still attempts safely.
  8. Each editor reaches the same core through MHP/companion, with accessible
     loading/failure/retry; unsupported native MCP and missing prerequisite
     surfaces are named waiting. Each product's qualification row names version,
     OS, transport, OAuth method, result cap and approval/Stop/revocation evidence.
- **Red drills** (restore source byte-exact and record each failure in
  `docs/certification/m124-<lane>.md`): drop strictness; skip host approval;
  reuse an approval or request after epoch change; authorize from an argument;
  mark a run read-only; duplicate dispatch on retry; turn unknown into success;
  bypass paid reserve/consent; pass a physical child action; bypass audience or
  grant revocation; emit a planted key through result/error/audit; disable audit
  before a write; throttle Stop behind a full queue; disconnect during approval;
  drop a native host's companion path; omit the command's Help row/lazy split.
- **Gates.** Delivery requires unweakened `npm run quality`, reference/l10n,
  host API, production bundle/split budgets, accessible UI, secret/SAST checks
  and OS/editor qualification. Tests use repository timeouts; slow fixture
  setup is shared, not excused with a command-line timeout. The local phase
  adds no npm dependency (§2 D3, 2026-10-09); a later phase that needs one
  checks peer ranges, exact pins and audit first.
- **Bundles.** Runtime-only `dist/connector.js` and remote/OAuth chunks load on
  use; own initial budget proposal 120 KiB aggregate connector Node
  code and 20 KiB approval UI, finalized by lane 0's measurements. Existing
  startup/deferred caps never rise; Node English fallback and lazy installed
  language propagation follow D6. No new activation import of connector code.
- **Certification checklist** (§6.0, plus):
  - [x] Dated primary-source research, proposed schemas/classes/scopes,
        local/remote architecture, editor parity, file ownership and red drills
  - [x] Owner questions in §3; missing orchestrator-link and outcome-contract
        dependencies named; docs-only formatting/hook receipts recorded in §7
  - [x] Local stdio phase (2026-10-09): contracts, lazy `mcp` entry, local
        grant, registry with unavailable states, our approval page, Stop path,
        scrub, audit, bounds, kill switch; client setup docs; tests and red
        drills
  - [ ] Contracts, adapters, local stdio, our approval UI, audit and limits
  - [ ] M110 home-node remote binding over the D90.8 link and the
        orchestrator-link contract, OAuth and per-device revocation
  - [ ] Every platform row qualified or named waiting with reason
  - [ ] Red drills, generated Help/docs, measured budgets, full quality green

but closing the windows needs an atomic store or a cross-process lock, and
neither the keychain binding nor the M109 vault port offers one. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/milestones.md](docs/plan-archive/milestones.md).

Reviews RVM123A3 (two P2 on m123/a4, Mac mini: a refusal-first loser keeps the
winner's rotation under the current generation via the sign-out count, and the
final Serve read races the caller's signal with the CLI reporting Cancelled)
and RVM123A4 (one logout barrier on m123/a5, Windows host: the generation is
written by Sign out only in one store write, each operation reads it once when
it begins, a refusal touches only the refused pair, a rotation replaces only
the pair it began from, with the full transition table, the joining rule and
the generation invariant; the sign-out count and the recovery are gone since
RVM123A4) stand in docs/certification/m123.md sections Lane A fixes II and
Lane A redesign II. The overlap is not closable over this store: in another
process, a Serve whose last generation read the store answered before Sign
out's write may return its bearer after that Sign out has returned, because
its check came first, and a store with no notification or lock cannot close
it. The residual windows (another process, two store calls, no
compare-and-swap) each lose a pair while none serves a pair issued before a
Sign out: Publish's checks versus its write, a take-back's compare versus its
delete, Refuse's compare versus its delete, Sign out's write versus its
delete, a crash between a write and its take-back, and a refresh whose last
caller cancels after GitHub rotated the pair. Full record:
[docs/plan-archive/milestones.md](docs/plan-archive/milestones.md).

  in M104's matrix. That means the same forms, drafts, confirmations, links,
  checks and held checkout as in VS Code, with Git run natively by the
  runtime and the GitHub token taken from D104's layered sources.
- **Depends on.**
  - M71 (released in 0.14.0) and D104.

    lanes 0, B and D). The F36 methods and `nativeGitHub.ts` come from
    `m104/pd-fix` once it merges, or lane L takes ownership of a copy, as
    M104 did with M98's token file.
  - M109's vault (an `oauth` item). While its broker is unavailable, the OS
    keychain through `keyStore.ts`.
  - M107's spawn admission (SPAWN017).
  - The owner's Q-M123, for the OAuth App. Nothing blocks on it before
    certification, because everything builds against the fake device-flow
    server.
- **Order.** Lane 0 first (one day). Then G, A, P and L run in parallel
  against lane 0's fakes. U follows once G's and P's ports answer. Q
  qualifies each editor as its route lands. D runs throughout. M123 starts
  after M104a's contract freeze, and does not block the 0.17.0 release.
- **Lanes and file ownership.** One integration branch, `feature/m123`,
  under M87's region rules. Engine roles follow D103:
  - Muse codes on the POSIX rigs.
  - Claude codes Windows-native work and the Visual Studio C#.

    it.

- **Record/checkout concurrency (FIXM123P3 redesign, 2026-10-09).** The
  third review round (RVM123P2: one P1, two P2s) showed patches could not
  close the races, so the record store and the checkout lifecycle were
  redesigned as one serialized owner per repository: a per-folder
  `revision`, validate → act → persist against the fresh state, a
  cross-window `mkdir` lock folder, and the batch child in its own process
  group with its own deadline. RVM123P3 found three P1s and two P2s left in
  that lock and lifecycle; FIXM123P4 below replaces both.
- **RVM123P8 repair (M123P9, 2026-10-09, win11).** Close the three P3
  findings without changing the fenced protocol: log a failed sweep listing
  where it is caught, with only the operation and a validated error code;
  use installed UI text for the uncertain-write error, translated in all
  fourteen tables; justify and register the two erased generic payload
  assertions. Add warning/privacy and translated checkout regressions,
  prove both against the old behavior and with byte-exact restored red
  drills, then run the complete lane P suites at repository timeouts and
  scoped static gates. Aggregate quality remains the lead's under the
  shared lane rules; no merge, push, paid/live calls or gate changes.
- **Record/checkout protocol (FIXM123P7 redesign, 2026-10-09; replaces
  FIXM123P4–P6).** The fourth review round (RVM123P6: three P2s) applied
  the third-round rule: the store and the checkout were rebuilt on one
  shared lock primitive, LOCKLIB (`src/core/locks/fileLease.ts`, with
  `nodeLeasePort.ts` and `processOwner.ts`), fenced reservations and one
  dispatch gate. Code: `src/runtime/panel/pullRequests/`
  (`recordGenerations.ts`, `records.ts`, `checkout.ts`, whose
  `PullRequestCheckoutProtocol` the service runs). Record:
  `docs/certification/m123.md`.

  | State   | Meaning                                                                                                     | Leaves via                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
  | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | absent  | no record; the folder is held by location anyway                                                            | `reserve` → pending                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
  | pending | a reserved checkout: a random `checkoutId`, its process (`pendingOwner`, with its boot), the writing fence  | `claim` → pending (claimed, the folder made under the same hold); `complete` → ready; `discard` → absent, once nothing it made is left; `supersede` → pending, when its folder is absent under the superseding hold and its process is provably gone or it is over an hour old |
  | ready   | finished; bound to `checkoutId`, `revision`, fence, head SHA and folder identity (`dev:ino` and birth time) | `release` with the card's single-use ticket for exactly that → trusted; `supersede` → pending (folder absent)                                                                                                                                                                  |
  | trusted | confirmed in the card                                                                                       | `supersede` → pending (folder absent); nothing restores an older record, and a failed checkout never brings trust back                                                                                                                                                         |

  | Step                | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
  | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | Lease (LOCKLIB)     | `worktree-records/lock` created with O_EXCL; its note names the owner (host, process id and birth, Linux boot), a random id, a renewal count and the lease (30 s). Each hold then takes a fence: `lock.fences/<n>`, created exclusively, above every earlier fence and every fence the records carry. `isHeldSync()`: the lease runs on the holder's monotonic clock, the lock file is this instance, the highest fence is this one. The note and fences are made visible, not forced to disk (a crash ends the lease); record generations are flushed. The note and fences are made visible, not forced to disk (a crash ends the lease; record generations are flushed).                  |
  | Renewal, release    | `renew()` rewrites the holder's own note in place only once the opened file itself shows this very instance (file id, birth time, note id, renewal: a reused file id is not enough), and holds only while its fence is still the highest after the write; `release()` retires only its own instance. Neither ever acts on a lock taken over from it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
  | Takeover            | only an instance (file id, birth time, note id and renewal) the waiter has itself watched, unchanged, for its holder's lease (never more than 30 s), on the monotonic clock, kept across attempts; early when the owner is provably gone (`processOwner.ts`) or the note is missing/torn for 2 s. One rename moves it aside; proven, it is removed; unproven for any reason (a read error, a mismatch), it is linked back while the name is free and the waiter waits on; if it cannot go back, the waiter ends busy and the moved file stays aside, never removed.                                                                                                                         |
  | Registry fence      | each hold reads the head and publishes at most once, a compare-and-swap: refused while the head's fence is not below the hold's, refused once `isHeldSync()` fails (checked synchronously just before the link), and the hard link of generation N+1 fails while N+1 exists. Every record written carries its hold's fence. Parent write ids and the one-record reconciliation stay as FIXM123P4 made them. A write that landed is never reported failed by what follows it (the sweep never throws; an unreadable proof leaves it unverified, then reconciled); one whose landing cannot be known comes back with every fence it may hold, and the checkout drops whichever its record is. |
  | Reservation         | a checkout id and the record's fence. `claim`, `complete` and `discard` are compare-and-swaps on it; `supersede` is one on the version read (checkout id, revision and fence) with the folder checked absent under the same hold.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
  | Claim               | under one hold: publish the claimed record (a new fence), then make the folder under a private name and rename it into place, which fails while anything is there. A refused claim makes nothing; a claim whose folder could not be made drops only its reservation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
  | Dispatch gate       | every git `checkout.ts` starts goes through `runGit` or `startGitBatch`, which call the gate and start the process in the same synchronous turn. The checkout's gate: trusted, not cancelled, and `holdsSync` (the record is still exactly this reservation). The cleanup's gate: trusted; refused, what this checkout made is removed without git and its registration is left to git's prune. File writes ask trust and Cancel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
  | Completion, failure | completion is a compare-and-swap on the claimed reservation. Refused or not known, the checkout removes exactly what it made (identity-checked; whole only once git added the worktree, else only while empty), then discards its own reservation. A failed checkout's record goes once nothing it made is left; one it could not remove stays pending, so the folder stays held.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
  | Checkout lifecycle  | a failure invalidates the file writers first, kills the batch tree, drains the writer in flight (5 s), then cleans up even after Cancel. A writer past its grace keeps the record pending until it stops and its cleanup has run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

  **What is proven, and how.** At most one window succeeds, no git runs
  for a window whose trust is gone, and the store never ends with a folder
  that no finished record of its maker names: every order of the
  protocol's await points (acquire, publish, link, make, git dispatch,
  remove), states reached again with the same history explored once, for
  two windows (with one or two holds stalling past their lease before or
  after their checks, trust revoked, a wall clock stepped at any point, a
  finished checkout whose folder is gone, the user's own checkout) and
  three windows (every order; and the taker's lease running out) —
  `test/unit/runtimePullRequestInterleavings.test.ts`, the real protocol
  and store logic over a registry that models the lease and generations.
  The model's I/O succeeds, except an injected fault: a publish that lands
  and then fails (one or two, at any link). That the file registry behaves
  as the model, its other I/O failures included (a sweep or proof that
  cannot list, a reconciliation that cannot read), is tested on real files
  (LOCKLIB's suite, the generation compare-and-swap, the forced-takeover
  property race, injected listing failures); renewal and its open-handle
  races are LOCKLIB's suite's, not the model's. "One owner" holds only where no lease runs out: a hold
  paused past its lease can leave both windows failed (never a folder
  without its record).

  **Residual window.** Same-user concurrent directory swaps stay outside
  the threat boundary (D104); the identity checks still detect them.
  Deleting the `worktree-records` folder by hand while a delayed writer is
  mid-write can let that writer's stale generation head the new history
  (deleting only the fences is recovered: holds go above the records'
  fence). On POSIX, the rename that puts a claimed folder in place
  replaces an _empty_ folder made in the instant between its presence
  check and the rename (no content is lost; Windows refuses). Clock steps:
  lease waits, leases and Linux births are immune; Windows and macOS
  births are the wall-clock time the kernel recorded at creation (macOS
  to the second; two births within 1 s are not told apart). The one
  wall-clock judgement left is the hour after which a pending checkout
  without its folder is recovered: a forward step can recover a live one
  early, whose claim or completion is then refused by the fence (it
  removes what it made); a backward step lengthens the wait. A file system
  that reports no birth time leaves identity to the file id alone, which
  Linux may reuse. A cleanup refused by trust leaves git's worktree
  registration for `git worktree prune`. Liveness: a live lock owner holds
  at most its 30 s lease, watched across attempts; a pending checkout
  waits until the lock frees or the person cancels it; a busy store is
  reported at once and waits the same way; a writer
  stuck in a system call that never returns keeps its record pending; a
  file system without hard links fails closed. Windows whole-tree
  retirement of the batch stays lane G's.

  **Lane G migration (M123G4, 2026-10-09).** Replaced the hand-rolled Git
  transaction lock with LOCKLIB: `renew()` every third of the 30 s lease,
  `isHeldSync()` beside the seal at every dispatch, and watched, proven
  retirement instead of the presence poll and newcomer wait. A removed or
  taken lock is never re-made. Certified RVM123G4's refresh/resume schedule:
  a paused old holder cannot reclaim a renewed successor or start another
  Git mutation. Already-running children may overlap after lock removal or
  lease expiry; fencing refuses subsequent payload dispatch, not an existing child.

  **Own renewal overlap (RVM123G4C, 2026-10-09).** LOCKLIB's synchronous
  hold check accepts its own old or next renewal count while renewal is in
  flight, with the same file id, birth, note id and current fence. A torn
  note counts as owned only during the opened file's accepted rewrite,
  within the unexpired lease. The Git wrapper defers latching an overlapping
  failed check until renewal settles and rechecks ownership then. Regressions
  pause the own-note write over an in-memory note port and native files,
  dispatch a real Git mutation, and retain successor/expiry/fence refusals.
  Simultaneous renewals recheck pending state after the ownership await
  (G132; numbered G83 until the RLM100 join, when that number was found shared); exactly one can enter its rewrite.

Lane G landed 2026-10-09 without the planned `src/core/git/process.ts` move: the host-API gate passes on the `src/host/git.ts` import (no `vscode` in its closure), so the lane kept the import and added `isUserEnvironment` to `GitProcessOptions` for the push and the fetch instead. No escape hatches; the record is `docs/certification/m123.md`.

Lane G repair (RVM123G, 6 P1 + 10 P2, 2026-10-09, branch `m123/g2`, Windows host). All sixteen findings fixed in one pass; each has a test that fails on `b9baa882d` and a red drill (`docs/certification/m123.md`).

- **`RuntimeGitDeps` grew** (lane 0's file, additive): `confirmPush` (M71's push modal: remote, masked URL, branch, target, commits), `pickRemote`, `userEnvironment` (D104's push/fetch exception) and the optional `admitWorkspaceCommand` (M72's admission). `ConversationGitPort` is unchanged.
- **The service binds the root at construction** (canonical path plus volume and file id) and refuses a link, junction or replacement folder at that path, at every operation and again at the spawn. The runner's `beforeRun` (after admission and the Windows job's preparation) rechecks the arguments, the operation's signal and owner, trust and the root's identity. Every method takes the caller's operation (signal and owner check); Cancel, a session change and disposal abort it. Mutations are serialized per physical repository across conversations in a process, each revalidating inside the lock (the commit stamp; the push re-planned and compared with what was confirmed). Two runtime processes on one repository still rely on git's own index lock between commands: a residual until the runtime has one owner per repository (M104's panel route). (Superseded by the third round below: a lock file shared across processes.)
- **Commit stamps** carry the status records (modes and index object names) and a SHA-256 of the unstaged and new files' bytes, read confined by identity (`confinedFiles.ts`: every ancestor a real folder before and after the open, the handle the file just seen). Draft prompts read new files the same way.
- **Redact before truncate:** the adapter redacts git's whole text before its cut; `createGitProcess` drops a partial last word of stderr once its cap cut it.
- **The terminal fallback** opens only for git's own failure of the confirmed push while the conversation still owns a trusted operation, with the resolved `gitPath` in the bound root.
- **Credentials:** the governed Windows job keeps `isUserEnvironment`; the standalone runtime keeps the Git routes it takes out at start (no `*_API_KEY`, no provider key) for the push and the fetch only (`src/runtime/gitUserEnvironment.ts`). `createGitProcess` takes an absolute `executable` (the resolved `gitPath`). (Superseded by the third round below: a named allow-list.)
- **Status:** porcelain-v2 `u` records are parsed past their ten fields. **Worktrees:** `pr-worktrees/` must be a real folder directly under the resolved data folder, checked before and at the spawn.
- **Wired:** the in-process route for a VS Code-family host without `vscode.git` (`conversationGitEntry.ts` picks `createRuntimeGit` when the extension is absent; `gitWindow.ts` supplies VS Code's push modal, remote pick, terminal, trust, hold and admission). Pull requests on that route wait for lane P. **Not wired:** every other editor (the runtime panel route is M104/lane U); the standalone runtime's `runtimeGitUserEnvironment` is that route's `userEnvironment`.

Lane G third round (RVM123G2, 6 P1 + 6 P2, 2026-10-09, branch `m123/g3`, Windows host): a redesign, not a patch, under D104's threat boundary (the lead's decision, recorded in D104). Record: `docs/certification/m123.md`, with the closure of all 28 findings of both reviews.

- **One bound pipeline** for every mutation: plan → confirmation → admission → final revalidation → spawn (D104). `src/runtime/panel/git/transaction.ts` holds the per-repository LOCKLIB lease (`GIT_TRANSACTION_LOCK_FILE` in git's common directory: exclusive create, a process-birth-bound holder, renewal every third of the 30 s monotonic lease, an increasing fence, watched takeover and proven retirement; a removed or taken lock is never re-made) and the seal (HEAD, the index, packed and loose refs, the reftable list, every configuration file git named, sampled before the revalidation, compared at the spawn). The in-process queue is gone (R7, R8).
- **Final revalidation after every wait:** inside the lock and the host's admission, the push plan is read again and compared whole (remote, every push URL from `git remote get-url --push --all` so a `pushInsteadOf` rewrite is shown and bound, refspec, target, upstream use, commit count, the branch's commit, the configuration files) and the commit stamp likewise; the seal then carries that to the spawn, after the runner's own admission and the Windows job's preparation (R2, R9). After `add -A`, what got staged must be what the form showed, or nothing is committed (the staging stays).
- **The spawn's last check** also runs at the Windows helper's payload authorization: `McpJobLaunch.authorize` is called on READY, and a refusal withholds GO, so the payload never starts (R1). It checks the root is a real directory (`lstat`, no link even to the same folder) with its bound identity (R10 detection), the lock still held and the seal intact.
- **Credentials:** an allow-list per operation; push and fetch get only `GIT_PUSH_CREDENTIAL_VARIABLES` on both launch routes, from the runtime's start capture, the service, the runner and the VS Code-family route, whose terminal opens with `strictEnv` in the same environment (R3). The terminal fallback opens only after `confirmedPushRoot` revalidated the bound repository and the plan (R5).
- **Confirmation text:** `maskRemoteUrl` masks every query value and fragment and judges the percent-decoded spelling too (R11).
- **Construction:** the root's identity is sampled synchronously when the service is made (R6 detection). **Tests** run git as their own identity with an isolated home and global configuration (R12).
- **Residuals under the boundary:** R4 (a same-user ancestor swap and restore around a path-based open), the windows R6 and R10 leave (host approval to construction; a swap of the root's own ancestors), a config include whose file is created between revalidation and spawn, a host that ignores `strictEnv`, and the pre-existing `dist/resourceGovernor.js` cap failure (also fails on the base).
- **Fix round (RVM123G3G, Grok: 0 P1, 2 P2, 1 P3).** The seal samples a link together with the file it leads to, so a linked configuration file rewritten behind an unchanged link refuses the push. The original presence poll and newcomer settle wait were superseded by M123G4's LOCKLIB migration after RVM123G4 proved a resumed old holder could reclaim a settled successor after its heartbeat. The lease now renews only its owned instance and checks its fence synchronously at dispatch; no lost lock is re-made. Already-running Git children may overlap after lock removal or expiry; only later dispatch is refused. The `pushInsteadOf` test now pushes through the rewrite and refuses when the rewrite changes during admission.

- **Acceptance per editor (all with fakes, no live calls).** The first
  available token source wins, and the user may sign in with any later one.

  | Editor                                         | Token sources, in order                                      | Git                                          | Panel                           | Exception |
  | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------- |
  | VS Code                                        | (a) VS Code's GitHub session; (b); (c)                       | the Git extension                            | webview                         | none      |
  | VS Code forks                                  | (a) where the fork ships GitHub sign-in; (b); (c)            | the Git extension where present, else native | webview                         | none      |
  | Arduino IDE 2                                  | (b); (c)                                                     | native (no `vscode.git`)                     | webview                         | none      |
  | JetBrains (with Android Studio)                | (a) the bundled GitHub plugin's account; (b); (c)            | native                                       | embedded (JCEF)                 | none      |
  | Visual Studio                                  | (a) if lane L finds a supported API; (b); (c)                | native                                       | embedded (WebView2)             | none      |
  | Eclipse (with Espressif IDE)                   | (b); (c)                                                     | native                                       | embedded (SWT browser)          | none      |
  | Zed, Xcode, Qt Creator, Neovim, Emacs, Sublime | (b); (c)                                                     | native                                       | companion                       | none      |
  | CLI                                            | (b), through `auth github login`, which prints the code; (c) | native                                       | companion (`panel --companion`) | none      |
  1. **The full path, in every editor above.** Sign in with each available
     source. Draft a commit message, commit, and push after the
     confirmation; each push-plan case is refused. Draft and open a pull
     request, as a draft and ready, including from a fork to its parent; an
     open pull request for the branch is linked instead of a second one.
     See its status and checks. Open someone else's pull request held,
     confirm trust, and see the hold lifted.
  2. **VS Code unchanged.** M71's suites pass, the harness screenshots are
     pixel-identical, and its token stays VS Code's.
  3. **The device flow, against the fake.** `authorization_pending`;
     `slow_down` (plus five seconds, never faster); `expired_token`;
     `access_denied`; `incorrect_device_code`; `device_flow_disabled`;
     `unsupported_grant_type`; a lost network. Cancel stops polling. A
     verification address other than GitHub's is refused.
  4. **The sources.** The order is honoured. `gh` is off by default, and
     refused from workspace scope. Leases expire. A 401 asks the user to
     sign in again. A missing `repo` scope is named.
  5. **Rule 8 drills.** Token canaries from each source are absent from MHP
     frames, companion responses, logs, the transcript, the vault audit,
     child arguments and environments (the push's included), problem
     reports and screenshots, checked by a grep test.
  6. **Held checkout.** RV71c's refusal table passes in every host, and a
     worktree made in one editor is held when another opens it.

- **Tests.**
  - Unit: the source order; the device-flow client (every code and timer,
    on a fake clock); the `gh` source (missing, signed out, scope missing,
    several accounts); the lease time limit and owner binding; the native
    Git adapter against the fixture repositories (a detached HEAD, behind
    upstream, a failing hook, a configured signer); the link store's bound;
    the scope header.
  - Integration: `test/e2e` drives `panel --stdio` with the fake host and
    the fake GitHub, and `--companion` with Playwright. The plugin
    harnesses test the lease: IntelliJ's `BasePlatformTestCase`, and the VS
    experimental instance.
  - Live: none without the lead. After Q-M123, there is one optional check:
    one device-flow sign-in by the owner and one draft pull request on a
    throwaway repository. It makes no model calls (the drafts are typed by
    hand), and it is counted and recorded.
- **Gates.**
  - The existing gates, with `check:editor-matrix` moving F36. The MHP
    schema snapshot takes the minor bump for `expiresAt`.
  - New guards with red drills, in `docs/certification/m123.md`: lease
    expiry, the verification-address check, the workspace-scope refusal,
    the push-environment rule and the token grep.
  - D6: the runtime panel entry is measured, plus 15%. The VS Code
    activation and Git bundle caps stay unchanged.
- **Security.**
  - **The token is never logged, returned or forwarded.** It is registered
    with the redactor for each request. MHP carries lease ids only, and the
    UI shows the source and the account's login, never the token.
  - **Leases** are UUIDs bound to their owner. They expire, and end at
    window close, a change of owner, shutdown and sign-out. Requests are
    limited to the origin, path and method allowlist.
  - **Scopes are minimal:** `repo`; `read:org` only on a proven need;
    nothing else.
  - **Storage:** a vault `oauth` item, origin-bound and hidden from agents,
    or the OS keychain. Never a file, a setting or a log.
  - **Revocation:** Sign out deletes the item and opens GitHub's revoke
    page. A 401 drops the token. A refresh rotates both tokens.
  - **Device-flow phishing:** only our panel shows a code; only GitHub's
    address is opened; a code from the model or a tool is never accepted.
  - **The `gh` source** is opt-in, from user or machine scope. Its token is
    held in memory for one request, and `gh` is resolved as `git` is (an
    absolute path, no shell).
  - **Agents never get the token.** `EXEC_CHILD_ENV_DROP` is unchanged, and
    the push gains no variable of ours.
  - **§9 residuals:** a same-user process can read the vault or keychain
    item, as it can VS Code's session (D89's residual). The `gh` source
    reads a token that `gh` already stores.
- **Size.** M overall:
  - 6–8k lines of TypeScript including tests (0 0.8k, G 1.8k, A 1.8k,
    P 1.8k, U 1.2k);
  - 0.6k of Kotlin;
  - 0.6k of C#, if Visual Studio has an API;
  - 1k of conformance scenarios.
    With five lanes in parallel, the critical path is lane 0, then P, U
    and Q.
- **Certification checklist** (§6.0, plus):

        fake id is recorded as the only blocker, at the top of the report.
        (Lane A, 2026-10-09.)
  - [ ] Lane 0's contract is frozen, with the schema snapshot.
  - [ ] A receipt per editor in `docs/certification/m123-<host>.md`; the
        matrix is generated; F36 is W in every row.
  - [ ] VS Code is unchanged (M71's suites and screenshots).
  - [ ] Rule 8 grep tests pass for each token source.
  - [ ] Every new guard has its red drill.
  - [ ] No live call without the lead; the optional live check is counted.
  - [ ] Codex reviews each lane class in one pass before push.

### DFACPERR — Honest ACP refusals (2026-10-10)

**Status 2026-10-10: built.** Certification:
`docs/certification/dfacperr-acp-refusals.md`. Review RVDFACPERR (round 1)
and this lane's round-2 repair of all seven findings (1 P1, 4 P2, 2 P3),
plus the same-day round-3 repair of review RVDFACPERR2's single P3, plus
the same-day round-4 repair of review RVDFACPERR3's three findings
(1 P2, 2 P3), round-5 repair of all RVDFACPERR4 findings (4 P2,
1 P3), and round-6 repair of review RVDFACPERR5's single P2 (a username
path segment refused its own unchanged export). Round 5 classifies invalid imported files
at their input boundaries (titles and bodies have no ceilings per D121),
preserves typed headless argument refusals, and
routes the native Prompt Library and panel initialization through the safe
catch and failed-promise eviction. Privacy adapters scrub account names only
in path segments or identity fields, preserving common words and structural
metadata. Regressions cover user/admin/test and a personal-looking username;
certification scopes names-only cause logging to its actual readers and
reruns the formerly timing-out lifecycle test at repository deadlines.

- **Scope.** Every ACP failure maps to the right JSON-RPC error with a
  product-owned, localized, privacy-safe message: defined refusals read as
  invalid request (-32600) with their own sentence, bad caller arguments as
  invalid params (-32602) with the flag that carried them, and genuine
  internal faults stay internal errors (-32603) with a fixed reason and no
  raw exception text in `error.data`. Exactly one `RequestError` identity:
  the engine owns the constructor; the lazy sharing bundle carries failures
  across as `AcpSharingFailure` (read with `isAcpSharingFailure`, never
  `instanceof`). Mode/model/effort commands against a backend session Muse
  Code evicted or closed read as a missing resource (-32002).
- **Out of scope.** Turn-path backend failures keep their terminal channel;
  schedules/estimate/reports/playbook-unbound paths keep their chat text;
  no new command, setting, string or dependency.
- [x] Sharing adapter carries no SDK copy; the engine maps bundle-crossing
      failures by name and code (P1), covered by an in-memory bundle test.
- [x] Caller-owned mini-zod validation fails as -32602 naming its flag;
      service-data validation stays internal (P2 validation).
- [x] `SessionNotLoadedError` on mode/model/effort reads as -32002 (P2 lifecycle).
- [x] Legal and vault catch-alls distinguish the defined refusal from
      genuine faults, which stay -32603 (P2 classification).
- [x] Unexpected sharing errors reach the wire sanitized; parser errors read
      in the installed language (P2 privacy, P3 localization).
- [x] Every fix has a regression test that fails without it and a recorded
      red drill with a byte-exact restore.
- [x] Unexpected sharing/prompt-store faults read as -32603 with the fixed
      could-not-complete reason and a server-side log entry, never as a
      prompt-file error (RVDFACPERR2 P3).
- [x] The server-side entry names the underlying fault (the failure rides
      as `cause`; RVDFACPERR3 P2), and headless `share`/`prompts` plus the
      editor prompt boundary keep defined refusals while reporting genuine
      faults as internal errors (RVDFACPERR3 P3).
- [x] Caller-file/schema/UTF-8 and malformed-draft refusals keep their
      localized reasons (titles and bodies have no ceilings per D121, so a
      draft that fails its schema reads as an invalid prompt file, never a
      size limit); native Library and panel initialization sanitize and
      retry;
      headless typed arguments retain their flag; common usernames preserve
      ordinary exports while complete path segments/identity fields remain
      scrubbed. Certification records the actual logging scope (RVDFACPERR4).
- [x] Every scrub marker is atomic from the single shared list, so the
      confirmation re-scrub is a fixed point and an unchanged username-path
      export releases in every format and mode (RVDFACPERR5 P2).

### Delivery order (2026-10-06)

The owner, 2026-10-05: "make sure you prioritize all of the remaining stuff
properly so smaller things get done quicker if able and in such a way that we
dont put the cart before the horse … do things in a proper logical order".

The rule: nothing starts before what it depends on, and where two items are
free to go, the smaller goes first. Each **Needs** below was read from that
milestone's own **Depends on** and lanes table. M113's plan reader (lane P)
reads this list for `/report project`'s next steps, so each entry keeps the
form `N. **Item** — reason. Needs: items.` Milestones already in a release
train, and those waiting on outside events, keep their own status lines.

1. **0.14.1** — in CI: the shell credential fence, the third startup diet and
   the badge fixes. Needs: nothing.
2. **0.14.2: the `/help` reference** (lane HELPREF) — small, and the owner
   asked for it as soon as possible; M112 to M115 add their rows to its
   `featureCatalog`. Needs: 0.14.1.
3. **M112: questions that never block** (D92) — small (about 48
   lane-hours), in 0.14.3, or folded into 0.14.2 when both are ready
   together. Needs: main only; its native-host, TUI and desktop rows wait for
   M104, M110a0 and M111b and block nothing.
4. **M118: prompt and chat sharing** (D98) — as soon as possible, at the
   front beside M112 and in parallel with it (about 34 lane-hours).
   Phase 1 ships in the next patch after 0.14.3, phase 2 (gists) in the
   one after. Needs: main; the native hosts' menus with M104, the TUI
   with M110a0's T, phase 3 with M110, M96, M113 and M115.

   modal and M88's lane C (timed sends). About 134 lane-hours; ships in the

### 6.0 Standard certification checklist (applies to every milestone)

- [ ] `npm run quality` exits 0 on a clean checkout (format:check, lint incl. lint:ps,
      typecheck, check:l10n, deadcode, cycles, duplication, test:unit with coverage
      thresholds, build with bundle budget, host globals and notices, security:audit,
      test:a11y, security:secrets, security:sast).
- [ ] Each new gate or test was seen to **fail** on a deliberate break, then
      pass again (record the break in the milestone notes).
- [ ] No new `eslint-disable`, `@ts-expect-error`, `as unknown as`, or `any`
      without an inline reason **and** a row in §8.
- [ ] No magic literals outside `src/shared/constants.ts` (and tests).
- [ ] No placeholder / mock / fallback code outside `test/**`.
- [ ] `README.md` updated for any new command, setting, or script; every
      documented command was run.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]`.
- [ ] Security review of new surfaces (inputs validated, secrets never logged,
      CSP intact, spawn args explicit).
- [ ] Visual milestones: screenshot or manual-check record in
      `docs/certification/<milestone>.md`.
- [ ] Commit with a message describing what changed and why.

#### M102 J review repair — FIXM102J (2026-10-05)

Repair all four RVM102J findings inside J's store, Node adapter and recorder.
Readers take the maintenance lock and verify its generation before returning;
a lost generation permits one fresh snapshot attempt, then an explicit failure.
Rollups are read through one open handle without a prior path-size bound, and
published with a private temporary file, fsync and atomic replacement (including
Windows rename retries). Lock claims use immutable numbered generations and
owner-token release markers: a predecessor never unlinks a successor's claim.
Claim paths also contain an immutable history epoch, published completely by
the existing exclusive-file helper. Reset chooses a new epoch, so delayed
predecessor cleanup cannot delete a reused generation in the new history.
Incomplete usage with a known price keeps `uncertain`, with the reported part
priced while missing counters stay absent. Each finding gets a deterministic
regression and a byte-exact guard-break drill in `docs/certification/m102-j.md`.
No new dependency or editor-specific behavior; all shared journal consumers
receive these fixes. Full quality and combined editor wiring remain lead/W work
as required by the rig brief; do not run full quality or merge in this lane.

### M6 — Sessions, history, rewind

**Status 2026-09-22: complete.** Certification record: `docs/certification/m6.md`.
Delivered as designed below: the History dialog (paged `session/list`,
grouped and searchable, archive in `workspaceState`, live through the
`sessionListStream` events), resume with inline/snapshot history replayed
into the transcript, the sidebar's ten-minute restore, rename and fork
(offered; Muse Code 1.3.0 refuses both on Windows and the panel shows the
refusal), the unread badge / tab mark, and the tab title following the
session name. Deviations from the design, all deliberate: a `none` history
(host budget) is reported as a warning notice rather than paged through
`view/page` (no session here has come close to the budget; the fallback
stays on the M8 polish list); pending approvals / questions listed in a
resume's `pendingRequests` are not re-shown (the host re-issues them as
server requests, which this client declines by design; a resumed session
with a decision pending is an edge the live check could not produce);
resume applies the surface's effort and permission mode to the session
instead of reading the session's own, so the composer never lies. Wire
probe (`scratchpad/probe-sessions.ts`, no tokens) against the day's live
sessions:

### M46 — Background work and stop; the `!` user shell; clarifying questions (D39)

**Status 2026-09-26: PR #33 merged into main at `e219d04` after local and hosted gates**
(`docs/certification/m46.md`). A full local gate passed on M45 base
`5581fe2` with the Windows accessibility runner capped at two workers;
M46 was then reconciled onto M45 candidates `502684c`, `ec5db58`,
`899b573`, `f5df625`, `4da43ac`, `f3390ec` and `ef84852`. The full local
quality gate passed on `ef84852`. M45 merged into main at `1908673`, whose
source tree is identical to `ef84852`; M46 now branches from that merge.
M46 was committed as `8a85d79` and opened as PR #33. Review found two
session-lifecycle gaps: final-surface disposal must stop CLI background
tasks, and resumed foreground shell history must restore the `Ctrl+B`
context. Both have focused failing-before/passing-after tests. The
corrected tree passed the full local gate. Its fresh review found one
more case: a Model API shell row starts before approval, so the running
shell shortcut stays off while the permission card waits. A real fake-API
and held-shell test failed before the change, passed after, and verifies
the shortcut works once approved. The second correction's local gate
passed. The next review found a running Model API `!` row missing from
another surface's history, and forks missing a background shell's terminal
context when the later note was cut. Both failed in focused tests before
the fixes; recording the running row and tagging terminal replay notes by
task fixed them. A cross-host restore test then caught that the started
`!` row needed a save at start; `touch()` persists it before completion.
The third correction passed the local full gate. The next review found
that a quiet foreground Model API shell was also absent from another
surface's live history. Started tool rows are now recorded once and
replaced by item ID when they move or finish; a focused test failed
before the change and passed after it. An unanswered function call is
deliberately not persisted to disk because its replay would lack an
output, so this guarantee is for surfaces sharing the live session. The
fourth correction passed the local full gate. A read-only review then
found that a second panel did not know about a shell approval already
pending in the shared Model API session, so its restored row could make
`Ctrl+B` intercept VS Code before the shell was runnable. The live
two-panel test failed before the change and passed after pending approval
requests were replayed to new listeners. The fifth correction passed the
local full gate. A second read-only review found that a joining panel in
Edit automatically could then approve a Manual panel's pending file edit.
Both Model API and Muse Code tests failed before the fix; replayed cards
now carry an internal marker that forbids automatic approval, including
Muse Code's `approval/listPending` path. The sixth correction passed the
local full gate. A further read-only review found the inverse live case:
an older Edit automatically surface could approve a new Manual surface's
edit. Both backends reproduced it; the Model API also exposed a pending
resolver registration race, fixed before the authorization drill. The
reverse order (Manual first, Auto joining) and two Auto panels proved a
single last-mode value cannot describe the shared session safely. Auto
approval now runs only while one controller holds it in Edit automatically;
detaching another panel restores it. The internal replay marker is removed
before postMessage. The seventh correction passed the local full gate.
Its review found one export gap: a Muse `userShell` ending by signal had
the signal in its row but not Markdown. The existing localized signal
label now appears in export too, with a failing-before/passing-after test.
The final export correction passed the local and current-head hosted
quality matrix, with no open review threads, before PR #33 merged.

- **Archived.** The full section is in [docs/plan-archive/milestones.md](docs/plan-archive/milestones.md).

### M71 — Git and pull requests (D49)

- **Archived.** The record that stood here is in [docs/plan-archive/milestones.md](docs/plan-archive/milestones.md).

**Status 2026-09-29: resumed** from unverified WIP `cfa2bc68` on
`feature/m71-git-prs`; the older gate on `3af80e40` does not certify this
tree. Current integration is isolated on `integrate/m71-resume-20260929`
and normally joins approved main `24ff09bc`, preserving the original WIP.
Its shared send path must retain M79's brief/todo rollback while admitting
only the current M71 draft generation. Fresh focused/negative proofs and
independent review precede root's complete exact-tree gates; all earlier
evidence remains historical. Complete the existing three-class review before integration: bind
commit and PR forms to their repository/branch/diffs, recheck trust and
conversation lifetime after awaits, stop later steps when Cancel closes a
form, name Git hooks/signers/credential helpers in consent, and require the
fetched PR head to match GitHub before creating its worktree. Keep the
existing API adapters, forms, GitHub captures and local Git fixtures;
no new dependency or design layer. Focused tests and disposable red drills
go in `docs/certification/m71.md`; latest-main integration, independent
review and full local/hosted gates remain required. Decisions taken in the build:

- **Archived.** The record that stood here is in [docs/plan-archive/milestones.md](docs/plan-archive/milestones.md).

- **Goal.** From finished work to an open PR without leaving the panel.
- **Scope.**
  - A generated commit message for the conversation's changes.
  - Commit and push go through VS Code's built-in git extension API, so
    the user's credential helpers and sign-in prompts apply (the
    extension's own git runs with no prompt and could not push).
  - Open a PR through VS Code's GitHub authentication, with a generated
    title and body, as a draft or ready. The confirmation shows the exact
    remote, branch, title and body, editable, with credential-shaped
    strings masked.
  - The PR is linked to its conversation, with its status and checks
    shown.
  - **A conversation in a worktree.** Its backend host is confined to the
    worktree (the Model API's workspace root; `muse serve` started in that
    folder), and the worktree is added as a workspace folder or opened in
    its own window as M32 does, so trust and language services apply to
    it. M77 reuses it.
  - "Open PR in a conversation" checks out the PR's branch in a
    worktree. A PR the user did not author is adversarial content until
    the user says otherwise:
    - its worktree is created under the extension's own storage and opens
      in its own window;
    - VS Code may still trust that folder, through a trusted parent (the
      home folder, say) or with workspace trust switched off, and the
      extension cannot ask VS Code about a folder before it opens. So the
      extension never relies on it: in that window it holds the
      conversation in Plan mode, with project rules, skills, hooks and MCP
      servers off (Muse Code starts without `--trust-workspace`), until the
      user confirms trust for that worktree in the extension's own card,
      whatever VS Code's trust says. Where VS Code opened it in Restricted
      Mode, that applies as well;
    - other extensions follow VS Code's own trust, which this extension
      cannot lower, and the card says so.
- **Rules.** Never force-push. Pushing and creating a PR always ask.
  GitHub only (D49, not taken). Unavailable in Restricted Mode.
- **Backends.** Both.
- **Acceptance.** No path force-pushes; every push and PR creation asks
  and shows what goes out; a PR by someone else opens held in Plan mode
  with its project configuration off until the user confirms trust in the
  extension's card, even when VS Code already trusts the folder; the
  worktree conversation cannot touch the main checkout.
- **Tests.** A fake git extension API and a fake GitHub endpoint, with a
  drill for the force-push refusal and the project-configuration switch.
- **Size.** M.

### M73 — Observation packing (D49)

- **Goal.** Long sessions stop resending large old tool outputs.

- **Archived.** The record that stood here is in [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

- **Status 2026-10-02: shipped off by default after its M75 run passed.**
  Built 2026-10-01 on
  `feature/m73-packing`, from M75's merged head. What is in it:
  - `src/core/backends/modelapi/observationPack.ts`: one session's store.
    An output over 8,000 characters rides whole for 2 requests, then as a
    placeholder (its call id, characters, lines, a token estimate, its
    first 4 and last 4 lines, bounded under the threshold); the swap is
    sticky, so the placeholder is the same text every request. A request
    counts once it is really sent, at the client's last step before
    `fetch` (`ResponseAttemptGuard.onRequestStarted`), and an HTTP retry of
    the same request counts once. `recall_output(id, offset)` pages the
    original back 4,000 characters at a time, never splitting a character;
    the replay keeps every original (placeholders never commit), so a
    restored session packs again from the whole outputs; a compaction
    forgets the store's originals and keeps the ledger.
  - The host builds the store only while its `observationPacking` dep is
    on and never for a subagent, which is also refused `recall_output`
    (a read-class tool: no card). The dep is read when a session is
    created or resumed: `museSpark.modelApiObservationPacking` (since its
    run passed, below) or the M75 arm.
  - The ledger rides on `tokenUsage` (`packedTokensAvoided`) to Account &
    usage's Tokens section, "Packing saved (estimate)", shown only while a
    session packs; the estimate is 4 characters a token, net of what the
    placeholder still costs.
  - The M75 side: the `packing` arm (`src/core/eval/mechanisms.ts`); two
    long-output tasks in the task set (`accept-long-middle-value`,
    `heldout-long-middle-rule`: a 512-record evidence file whose middle
    record is needed after two more requests), so the set is twelve tasks,
    seven accept and five held-out, under the same 0.75 floors (6 of 7, 4
    of 5); results record the ledger and successful recalls; the live run
    passes only if packing engaged on every long-output task it ran
    (`unengagedLongOutputTasks`).
  - **Not built: the Evidence-Preserving Reducer.** The evaluation refuses
    every paid use (D48), so it cannot measure a paid reducer, and the gate
    forbids shipping what is not measured (§3).
  - **The M75 run passed (2026-10-02, after the RV73 repairs):** both
    arms 7/7 accept and 5/5 held-out against the 0.75 floors, packing
    engaged on both long-output tasks, 111 model calls on the contributor
    model for $0.0156 (`docs/certification/m73-run.md`). On the long-output
    tasks packing sent 39% fewer input tokens at about the same cost: what
    it leaves out was mostly read from the cache. So, as the gate says,
    the setting was added, off by default and machine-scoped:
    `museSpark.modelApiObservationPacking` (VS Code only; the ACP agent
    does not pack).
  - The WIP of `integrate/m73-m75-join-20260930` (staged tree `d52b6a9a`)
    is archived as `_archive-2026-10-01/m73-m75-join-wip`; what was kept
    and dropped is in `docs/certification/m73.md`.

- **Archived.** The record that stood here is in [docs/plan-archive/decisions.md](docs/plan-archive/decisions.md).

**Status 2026-10-21 (RLM77 recovery): building.** The three source

each attempt's spend in the run. C-M77-3: bindings for JetBrains, Visual
Studio, Eclipse, Zed, Xcode, Neovim, Emacs, Sublime and ACP/headless.
C-M77-4: three-OS/editor qualification and independent review. The source
lane's VS Code-only implementation is not an approved scope reduction.
